title: Internal Auditor – Contracting Operations
description:
Job Purpose:

To support the Head of Internal Audit in providing independent assurance over the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management, and governance processes across the Group’s contracting businesses. The role will focus on project execution, procurement, cost control, subcontractor management, and compliance with approved policies, DOA, and contractual obligations.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Audit Planning & Execution

  • Execute risk-based internal audits across contracting operations, including project sites and head office functions
  • Perform end-to-end audits covering:

Ø Project lifecycle (bidding, estimation, execution, and closure)

Ø Procurement and subcontractor management

Ø Cost monitoring, budgeting, and variation orders

  • Identify control gaps, inefficiencies, and areas of financial or operational risk

2. Project & Cost Control Audits

  • Review project budgets versus actual costs and investigate variances
  • Assess controls over:

Ø Material usage and wastage

Ø Labor cost allocation

Ø Equipment utilization

  • Evaluate the integrity of project reporting and cost-to-complete estimates

3. Procurement & Contract Management

  • Audit procurement processes to ensure compliance with policies and DOA
  • Review vendor selection, tendering processes, and contract awards
  • Evaluate subcontractor agreements, billing, and performance monitoring
  • Identify risks of overpricing, conflict of interest, or non-competitive sourcing

4. Compliance & Governance

  • Ensure adherence to approved Policies & Procedures, DOA, and Management Memos
  • Review exceptions and confirm proper approvals are obtained (CEO/Chairman where applicable)
  • Assess regulatory and contractual compliance within project execution

5. Site Audits & Operational Reviews

  • Conduct periodic site visits to verify:

Ø Physical progress vs reported progress

Ø Inventory and material controls

Ø Site-level compliance with policies and safety procedures (high-level review)

  • Identify operational inefficiencies and leakages at site level

6. Reporting & Follow-Up

  • Prepare clear, concise audit reports highlighting key risks and actionable recommendations
  • Track implementation of audit recommendations and report status to Head of Internal Audit
  • Escalate critical findings and control weaknesses in a timely manner

7. Advisory Role

  • Provide practical recommendations to improve processes without compromising independence
  • Support management in strengthening internal controls and operational efficiency
  • Assist in developing and updating audit programs specific to contracting business risks

Key Skills & Competencies:

  • Strong understanding of contracting/construction business processes
  • Practical knowledge of project costing, BOQs, and contract management
  • Risk-based audit approach with attention to detail
  • Ability to work independently and conduct site audits
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Effective communication and report writing skills
  • High level of integrity and professional skepticism


Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Accounting, Finance, or related field
  • Professional certifications preferred (e.g., CPA, ACCA, CIA, or equivalent)
  • 5–8+ years of experience in: Internal Audit / External Audit with contracting exposure, or Commercial / Cost Control / Project Finance roles within contracting companies
  • Experience in ERP systems (e.g., Oracle, SAP, or similar) is an advantage

title: Mill Trainer
description:
We are IAMGOLD. Innovative, Accountable Mining.

IAMGOLD is a Canadian-based gold mining company with operations and development projects across North America and West Africa. With flagship operations such as the Côté Gold Mine in Ontario—one of Canada’s largest and most technologically advanced gold mines—we’re not just mining gold; we’re shaping the future of mining.

We believe mining can be different. By combining innovation with a strong commitment to sustainability and accountability, we create lasting value for our people and the communities where we operate. At IAMGOLD, when we engage, empower, and support each other, we create extraordinary outcomes—delivering value for our people, partners, and stakeholders while building stronger, more resilient communities.

At Côté Gold, we’re leading the way in modern mining. With an 18+ year mine life, Côté Gold will inject C$5 billion in wages into the economy and create lasting benefits for the region. Over 600 full-time jobs and strong partnerships with Mattagami and Flying Post First Nations mean you’ll be part of something bigger—building prosperity and progress for generations. Industry leaders call us “a model for modern mining and sustainability”, and you can help write the next chapter.

Want to Learn More About IAMGOLD?

  • Check out the IAMGOLD Blog

  • Read about our Côté Gold

    About the role\:


    We are actively seeking 2 Mill Trainers who will be responsible for delivering, coordinating, and continuously improving mill operations training at Côté Gold. This role supports safe, compliant, and efficient mill operations by developing employee capability through classroom instruction, field-based coaching, practical assessments, and documented competency verification. The Mill Trainer works closely with Mill Operations, Maintenance, Safety, and the Training team to support onboarding, employee progression, Ontario Mill Common Core and site-specific requirements, and ongoing operational readiness. This position plays a key role in building a strong safety culture, closing training gaps, and ensuring employees have the knowledge, skill, and confidence to perform their work safely and effectively.


    These roles are located at the Côté Gold Mine Site and report to the Training Supervisor on a day/night rotation.

    Responsibilities\:

    • Coordinate and deliver mill operations training, including classroom, practical, control room, field-based, and site-specific training.
    • Assess and verify employee competency through observation, practical evaluations, field follow-ups, and documented feedback.
    • Support employee progression through mill circuits and applicable Ontario Mill Common Core and site-specific modules.
    • Mentor, coach, and support operators in safe, consistent, and efficient mill practices, including control room, field operations, process equipment, mobile equipment, and emergency response expectations as applicable.
    • Work with Mill Operations, Maintenance, Safety, Training Supervisors, trainers, and subject matter experts to identify priorities, close gaps, and ensure training supports operational needs and risk controls.
    • Develop, review, and update training materials, lesson plans, assessments, procedures, and practical sign-off tools to align with current operating standards.
    • Maintain audit-ready training records, reports, competency documentation, and certification data in accordance with legislative and company requirements.
    • Coordinate or support vendor and OEM training as required for mill equipment, process control systems, mobile equipment, and specialized operational needs.
    • Support continuous improvement by identifying gaps in training programs, procedures, and operational practices, and contributing to practical solutions.
    • Promote safety leadership and operational excellence by participating in safety initiatives, investigations, and cross-functional teamwork.

  • Experience deploying, scaling, and managing service meshes, microservices releases, and containerized AI model deployment frameworks (e.g., vLLM, Triton Inference Server, Hugging Face TGI).

  • Expert knowledge of Git, including advanced branching strategies (GitFlow, Trunk-Based Development), repository management, and managing version control for application code, configuration, and prompt templates.

title: QC Executive – Diagnostics Reagents
description:
Job Title: Quality Control Executive – Diagnostics Reagents

Location: Hyderabad, India

Department: Quality Control

Experience: 2–5 years (QC in IVD reagents / clinical chemistry)

Employment Type: Full-time, on-site

About Arni Medica

Arni Medica Private Limited is an ISO 13485:2016 and ISO 9001:2015 certified medical device and in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) manufacturer based at the Medical Devices Park, Sangareddy (Hyderabad), Telangana. We design and manufacture nephrology, infusion therapy, respiratory care and surgical disposables, and are building a full IVD diagnostics franchise spanning clinical chemistry, electrolyte/ISE, blood gas (ABG), fluorescence immunoassay (FIA) and chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) platforms — backed by Class 100K/10K cleanrooms, EtO sterilization and a CDSCO manufacturing licence (MFG/MD/2023/000942).

Role Overview

The QC Executive will perform raw-material, in-process and finished-product testing for diagnostics reagents to ensure compliance with approved specifications and product performance. The role also supports method validation, stability studies and investigation of atypical results.

title: Injection Molding Engineer - Medical Devices
description:
Arni Medica Private Limited, an ISO 13485:2016 certified medical devices and IVD manufacturer at the Medical Devices Park, Hyderabad, is hiring Injection Molding Engineers to own molding process engineering, mold care and validation for precision medical device components manufactured in a cleanroom environment.

Roles & Responsibilities

  • Establish robust, repeatable process windows using scientific/decoupled molding principles; define and document process parameters for every mold and material.
  • Lead machine and mold setup standards: changeover procedures, startup/shutdown sequences and settings sheets for hydraulic, electric and hybrid machines with auxiliary equipment.
  • Drive troubleshooting and root-cause analysis (5-Why, fishbone) of molding defects, dimensional drift, cycle time losses, rejection and unplanned downtime; implement corrective and preventive actions.
  • Own the preventive and predictive maintenance program for medical device molds: PM schedules, hot runner and ejector system maintenance, cavity/core polishing standards, spare parts planning, mold history and shot-count tracking; manage external toolroom repairs.
  • Lead process validation (IQ/OQ/PQ), mold qualification trials, first article inspection and capability studies with QA/RA; support CAPA, deviations and change control for molding processes.
  • Support new mold trials, new product introductions and mold transfers; review mold designs (cooling, venting, gating, hot runners) with toolmakers for manufacturability and maintainability.
  • Ensure GMP and cleanroom (ISO Class 7/8) discipline, line clearance, 5S, LOTO and machine safety; maintain DHR-linked records per ISO 13485.
  • Train and supervise technicians and operators on machine handling, process discipline and mold care; track OEE, rejection and downtime metrics and drive continuous improvement.

Qualifications

  • Diploma or B.Tech in Plastics, Polymer, Mechanical or Production Engineering; CIPET background preferred.
  • 4 to 8 years in injection molding, including process engineering, mold maintenance and validation exposure.
  • Experience in medical device, IVD or other precision/cleanroom molding is a strong advantage.
  • Working knowledge of medical grade polymers (PP, PE, ABS, PC, PVC, TPE) and machines such as Arburg, Engel, Toshiba, Haitian or Ferromatik Milacron.
  • Strong documentation skills: engineering drawings, measurement systems, validation protocols and reports in English; comfortable with Excel/MIS.

description:

Roles and Responsibilities​

  • Work effectively in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities and multiple parallel requirements.



Must-Have Skills and Experience
​

Status\: Full Time
Hours\: 37.5 hours per week
Faculty/Department\: Capital Development & Facilities Management
Campus/Location\: North Campus
Minimum Starting Salary\: $107,449; starting salaries are determined based on qualifications and years of related experience.

About the Capital Development & Facilities Management Department at Humber\:
Capital Development & Facilities Management is responsible for new construction and renovation projects and provides project design, planning and space allocation services to improve and expand Humber's campus environment. We maintain all college buildings and grounds to provide a safe, clean, healthy and well-maintained campus environment that supports well-being and promotes excellence in teaching and learning at Humber. We also lead the college’s sustainability programs through the Office of Sustainability.

About the Role\:

The Energy Engineer will support Humber’s overall climate action and energy efficiency objectives with a
specific focus on improving the efficiency of its existing building stock of over 3M ft2 over two main campuses.

The Energy Engineer will identify, assess, prioritize, recommend and implement opportunities for energy
savings and greenhouse gas emissions reductions of mechanical and electrical building systems. This will
include project management for the delivery of medium sized construction projects. Existing infrastructure and
systems (Building Automation System, Energy Management Information System, Lighting Control System,
Energy Analytics & Fault Detection System) will also be utilized to uncover anomalies in operational data;
corrective actions will be implemented in conjunction with the operations teams or capital projects.

Duties Include, but limited to

  • Building Optimization\: Identify, assess, prioritize, recommend and implement energy saving opportunities related to operational changes. Engage with the operations team and departments as necessary. Work to create and foster a sustainable energy management culture.
    • Lead the implementation and development of the SkySpark platform; Humber’s energy management and fault detection system that integrates BAS, metering and lighting controls data into one system;
    • Carry out the review of Building Automation System and control sequences to identify opportunities and implement changes for control optimization;
    • Create and regularly analyze trend logs from the Siemens Building Automation System;
    • Gather operational performance data to assess equipment operation and identify deficiencies and opportunities for improvement;
    • Create data visualizations to quickly analyze hundreds of thousands of data points;
    • Develop dashboards to benchmark and monitor energy consumption and key performance metrics;
    • Lead the administration, maintenance and expansion of Niagara Based Energy Management Information System and SkySpark Energy Analytics platform;
    • Identify, assess, prioritize and recommend energy-saving initiatives, including preparing business cases to support capital expenditures
  • Energy Projects\: Identify, assess, prioritize, recommend and implement opportunities for energy saving capital projects. This will include preparation of business cases to justify capital expenditures. Act as a resource to project teams for planned renovation projects.
    • Project management of energy efficiency projects (<$250K), including project planning, tendering, proposal review, scheduling, project supervision and coordination, technical content and review, commissioning, close out and invoicing;
    • Support planned building renovations and maintenance projects as a subject matter expert to maximize opportunities for energy efficiency.
  • Measurement and Verification\:
    • Develop reporting process for annual reports to Senior Management on Key Performance Indicators in the overall performance of the College’s energy plans;
    • Execute weather correction calculations that address weather sensitivity and seasonality;
    • Perform measurement & verification activities on individual sub-projects to verify savings and inform future projects.
  • Incentives\: Coordinate incentive applications with local utility providers
  • Education & Awareness\: Promote initiatives and successes to internal and external community to position Humber as a leader in energy efficiency. This includes presentations at conferences, academic engagement, writing technical papers, and hosting events and tours for peer organizations and industry.

title: CAD and Simulation Engineer
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

CAD and Simulation Engineer

Product Design, Digital Simulation and AI Environments

Location:

New Delhi

Employment Type:

Full-time

Experience Level:

2-4 Years

Department:

Engineering / Mechanical Design & Simulation

Role Purpose

The engineer will convert product and system requirements into manufacturable mechanical designs and credible digital models. The position requires practical ownership of CAD, design for manufacture, structural and fluid analysis, simulation validation, AI training environments, and simulator integration with hardware, firmware, controls, and autonomy teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Mechanical CAD: Create parametric parts, assemblies, mechanisms, enclosures, mounts, frames, fixtures, and production drawings with controlled revisions and clear design intent.

  • Prototype design: Design parts for additive manufacturing, machining, sheet fabrication, and rapid assembly while accounting for tolerances, supports, orientation, finishing, and iteration speed.

  • Production design: Develop parts for injection moulding and other scalable processes, including draft, wall thickness, ribs, bosses, undercuts, parting lines, ejector access, tooling constraints, and assembly features.

  • Engineering definition: Apply material selection, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, tolerance-stack analysis, fastening, sealing, surface finish, fit, and serviceability requirements.

  • Structural simulation: Perform finite-element analysis for stress, strain, displacement, contact, buckling, fatigue, vibration, thermal stress, safety factors, and stress-relief design features.

  • CFD and thermal analysis: Model airflow, pressure drop, cooling, heat transfer, fluid forces, and environmental conditions; refine mesh, boundary conditions, and assumptions to support design decisions.

  • Simulation validation: Define load cases, simplify geometry responsibly, assess convergence and sensitivity, compare results with calculations or tests, and document model limits.

  • AI training environments: Build physically credible 3D scenes in Unreal Engine, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, or similar platforms with terrain, lighting, materials, collision, sensors, assets, scenarios, and synthetic-data outputs.

  • System simulator development: Create software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop simulators that model vehicle, robotic, sensor, actuator, communication, environmental, and operator behavior.

  • Cross-functional delivery: Work with mechanical, electronics, firmware, controls, autonomy, testing, manufacturing, and field teams to review interfaces, resolve faults, and maintain shared models and evidence.

Core Technical Areas

Area

Expected Knowledge and Application

CAD modelling

Parametric solid and surface modelling, large assemblies, mechanisms, configurations, design tables, drawing release, revision control, and CAD data exchange.

Manufacturing design

Design for additive manufacturing, machining, sheet fabrication, injection moulding, assembly, tooling, inspection, maintenance, and cost-effective production.

Mechanical definition

Materials, fits, fasteners, seals, geometric tolerances, datum schemes, tolerance stacks, surface finishes, clearances, and interface control.

Structural FEA

Meshing, contacts, constraints, load cases, linear and nonlinear response, stress and strain, deflection, buckling, fatigue, vibration, and result validation.

CFD and thermal

Fluid domains, turbulence models, heat transfer, rotating or moving regions, pressure loss, cooling performance, mesh independence, and correlation with tests.

AI environments

Unreal Engine and Isaac Sim scene construction, USD assets, materials, collision, sensor models, synthetic data, domain randomization, and ground-truth generation.

System simulation

Real-time physics, vehicle or robot dynamics, actuator and sensor models, scenario control, telemetry, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and operator interfaces.

Programming and tools

Python and C++ for simulation logic, automation, data processing, integration, and test tooling, together with real-time platform scripting or visual scripting.

Preferred Experience

title: Content Strategist & Writer
description:
We know things worth saying — about the product, about our customers, about why training providers pick us over the alternatives. Almost none of it ever leaves the room. It lives in founder conversations, sales calls, and product Slack threads, and then it just sits there. We need someone who can take that and turn it into something the rest of the world can actually read.

Now, for you who don't know Blend-ed — we're an AI-first LMS built on Open edX, one of a small number of official global Open edX partners. We work with training providers and corporate clients across the globe, with some genuinely strong logos already on our shelf, delivering high-stakes training that people actually depend on.


What you'll actually be solving

We have more good ideas than published content. Founders talk to customers every week and learn things worth saying — but nobody's turning that into an article, a page, a case study, or a campaign. That's the gap. You don't wait for a brief with every step mapped out; you take a rough thought or a customer insight and carry it all the way to something published and working.

  • Turn a founder conversation, a product update, or a sales call into content — decide the objective, the audience, the format, and get it made.

  • Build the plan, not just the pieces. Turn what we know about the business and the audience into themes, campaigns, and an editorial calendar with real deadlines and owners.

  • Write the actual thing — website copy, articles, case studies, emails, social, sales material — whatever format the point actually needs.

  • Own it through to live. Brief, draft, review, coordinate with design and product, publish, and check that the final version is right.

  • Give it a life beyond one channel. One customer conversation should become an article, an email, and a handful of posts — each shaped for where it lands, not copy-pasted.


What you'll do in your first 90 days

(These are our proposed milestones — we'd shape the exact targets with you in week one.)

  1. Take stock of what exists. Go through our current content, messaging, and channels — flag what's working, what needs fixing, and what's missing entirely.

  1. Build a real editorial calendar. Turn business priorities and audience needs into an actual plan, not a wish list.

  1. Ship the first pieces. Take a small set of ideas through research, writing, and publishing — prove you can carry something from "we should talk about this" to live.

  1. Set up a repeatable workflow. Build the process for collecting ideas, briefing, reviewing, and publishing on time, so it doesn't depend on you personally holding it all together.

  1. Learn what's actually working. Look at early results and feedback, and tell us honestly what to double down on, fix, or drop.


What we're looking for

You've done this before (non-negotiables)

  • You can really write — structure an argument, explain an idea clearly, and make every paragraph earn its place. Excellent written English, since you're writing for a global audience.

  • You've taken content from strategy to a finished, published result — not just drafts that sit in a doc.

  • You work independently. You ask the right questions, make reasonable calls without needing every step handed to you, and keep things moving.

  • You can pull real information out of people — interviewing, research, fact-checking — and turn an unfamiliar topic into something accurate.

  • You get that a founder, a training provider, and a product user need the same idea explained differently.

You might also bring (differentiators)

  • You know your way around SEO and distribution — search intent, content structure, making things discoverable without sacrificing readability.

  • You've written for B2B SaaS, LMS, ed-tech, or corporate training before.

  • You have a portfolio that shows both the content and the thinking behind it.

  • You've written case studies or sales-supporting content, or briefed designers on visual/video work.

  • You use AI tools well — with your own judgment doing the fact-checking and editing, not the tool.


Why this role matters

We're about 20 people building a product and having customer conversations every day, and most of what we learn never leaves the building. You're the one who closes that gap — turning what we know into something a buyer outside Blend-ed can actually read, understand, and act on.

There will always be more good ideas than time to execute them. Your job is picking the ones worth pursuing and carrying them all the way through — from "we should talk about this" to something published, used, and still working for us months later.

title: Request for Proposals : Adapting the Means Testing Methodology
description:
About CHANCEN International

Submission Deadline: 12th October 2026

Chancen International is a non-profit financial institution providing ethical, fair, and responsible financing to help young Africans access quality tertiary education. Using an innovative Income Share Agreement (ISA) model, we cover students' tuition fees, allowing them to study without financial barriers. Graduates repay a portion of their income once employed, creating a sustainable funding cycle that supports future generations. By empowering young people with education, we enable their transition to meaningful employment, fostering economic mobility and strengthening communities.

Headquartered in Kigali, Rwanda, and operating in Rwanda, Kenya, South Africa, and Ghana, Chancen International has helped over 11,000 young people access education leading to dignified work. Our focus on marginalized populations ensures these youth gain the skills needed to thrive and contribute to building strong economies and peaceful nations.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive working environment where each individual can flourish and achieve their full potential. Our actions are guided by our company values: Authenticity, Curiosity, Courage, Stewardship and Fairness.


Background and Objective

Chancen's means testing methodology, developed and validated in Rwanda, is used to assess applicants' socioeconomic status and determine eligibility for our Income Share Agreement financing. As we expand our reach in South Africa and Kenya, we need this methodology Chancen invites qualified organizations and individual consultants with relevant expertise to apply to support this adaptation, ensuring the methodology remains rigorous, locally grounded, and fit for purpose in both countries. Applicants may apply to work on one country or both, please indicate clearly in your proposal which country/countries you are applying for.

Scope of Work

The selected organization(s) or consultant(s) will adapt Chancen's existing methodology and scoring tool for South Africa and/or Kenya, preserving its overall structure and logic while ensuring indicators, thresholds, and data sources fit local realities.

The assignment includes:

  • Reviewing the existing methodology and tool, and assessing fit and gaps for the country/countries applied for.

  • Identifying appropriate national data sources to inform country-specific thresholds.

  • Recommending and justifying adapted indicators and thresholds for each country applied for.

  • Updating the scoring tool and methodology note for each country applied for.

  • Supporting Chancen's MEL team to test and validate the adapted tool(s) ahead of roll-out.

Expected Deliverables

Per country applied for:

  • Inception note confirming approach, data sources, and timeline

  • Country methodology note documenting adapted thresholds and rationale

  • Adapted scoring tool, mirroring the structure of the existing tool

  • Validation summary and final handover, including a short presentation to Chancen's leadership and MEL team.






Requirements

Required Qualifications and Experience:

Chancen welcomes applications from both organizations (research firms, consultancies, academic/policy research centers) and individual consultants able to demonstrate:

  • Experience designing or adapting means testing, targeting, or proxy means test methodologies — ideally in education, social protection, or development finance.

  • Familiarity with household living standards, income/expenditure, or multidimensional poverty measurement, and with South Africa's and/or Kenya's household survey landscape.

How to apply:
​

Submit the following by 12th October 2026 combined into a single file:


  1. A cover note stating whether you are applying for South Africa, Kenya, or both.

  2. A brief technical proposal (max. 3 pages) outlining your proposed approach to means testing/proxy mean test methodology design, relevant data sources you would use, and how you would validate the tool for the country context.

  3. A CV (individuals) or company profile with team CVs (organizations).

  4. At least two references or examples of similar past work, ideally relevant to the country/countries applied for.

  5. A financial proposal / cost estimate (separate line items per country if applying for both).



Benefits

​​

Engagement Officer, The Calanais VISITOR CENTRE
22.5 hours Per week, permanent contract

£31,827 fte (£19,096 pro rata) per annum

job description

ROLE OVERVIEW

About the Calanais Visitor Centre

At the Calanais Visitor Centre, we are committed to preserving, researching, and sharing the rich archaeological heritage of the Calanais Standing Stones. Our vision is to create an outstanding visitor experience while maintaining a deep connection between the site, the community, and the wider world.


We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer that celebrates diversity, operates within a culture of respect, and creates a welcoming environment for all employees.


Role Purpose


Support the Heritage Manager with heritage and communication activities that help people connect with Calanais. You will promote the Centre and its programmes, strengthen community connections and support the visitor experience.

Normal working days are three days per week, Monday to Friday, with flexibility to agree which days are worked. Occasional evening and weekend work may be required to support events and operational needs.


Reports to: Heritage Manager

Direct Reports: N/A


Who We're Looking For


We’re looking for an enthusiastic and organised individual with a passion for bringing the heritage of Calanais and the Outer Hebrides to life. Working closely with the Heritage Manager, you’ll help develop and deliver an engaging heritage programme that connects visitors and local communities with the site’s rich history. You’ll bring strong interpersonal and project delivery skills, a collaborative approach to building partnerships, and a commitment to diversity, inclusion and accessibility through our Heritage for All programme. You’ll champion Gaelic culture and language, confidently represent the Centre at events and public engagement opportunities, and use visitor feedback to help shape and improve our activities. Experience in heritage, community engagement or partnership working, alongside Gaelic language skills, would be welcome but is not essential.



This role would suit someone who:

  • Has a passion for culture and heritage
  • Takes pride in being organised, accurate and highly dependable.
  • Is confident managing multiple priorities while remaining calm under pressure.
  • Has a keen eye for detail and enjoys producing work of a consistently high standard.


Requirements

Roles and Responsibilities

Heritage Programme Delivery

  • Develop and deliver aspects of the heritage program in partnership with the Heritage Manager.
  • Promote diversity, inclusivity, and accessibility through the heritage for all programme, fostering an environment where all voices are heard and valued.
  • Ensure that gaelic culture and language are championed throughout our activities.
  • Develop and maintain effective partnerships with community groups, heritage organisations, archaeologists, educational institutions, tourism bodies and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate the collection and management of visitor feedback through surveys, observation logs and evaluation activities.

Communications, Marketing and PR

  • Create engaging, accurate and accessible content that communicates the significance of the Calanais Standing Stones and the wider heritage of the area.
  • Support the delivery of the centre's communications and marketing plan in collaboration with the heritage manager.
  • Coordinate media enquiries, press releases, online reviews, key marketing assets and affiliate websites and promotional campaigns in line with organisational priorities.

Other Responsibilities

  • Commit to continuous professional development and undertake relevant training.
  • Keep up to date with developments in communications, digital engagement and the heritage sector.

Person Specification

Essential Skills, Experience and Qualifications

  • Excellent organisational, planning and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience of planning and delivering projects within agreed budgets and timescales.
  • A genuine enthusiasm for promoting heritage, culture and visitor engagement.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with exceptional attention to detail and proofreading ability.

Desirable Skills, Experience and Qualifications

  • Ability to speak Gaelic.
  • Qualification in communications, marketing, heritage, event management or a related discipline.
  • Experience of working within the heritage, tourism, culture or charitable sectors.

Personal Attributes

  • Able to work effectively as part of a small team while also being confident working independently.
  • Creative, enthusiastic and proactive, with the ability to develop innovative ways of engaging audiences.
  • Flexible, adaptable and willing to support a wide range of organisational activities.


Benefits

WHAT WE OFFER

At the Calanais Visitor Centre, we believe in creating a supportive, rewarding, and inspiring workplace. We offer:

· Competitive Salary & Benefits – Including a comprehensive benefits package.

· Fair Work Scotland Accreditation – Commitment to being a Living Wage employer and promoting Fair Work principles.

· Personal & Professional Development – Ongoing training, leadership development, and opportunities for career growth.

· Work-Life Balance – A flexible and supportive work environment that prioritises employee wellbeing.

· Recognition & Reward – A culture that values contributions and celebrates achievements.

· An Inclusive & Supportive Workplace – A welcoming and dynamic environment where employees feel valued and empowered to grow.

Join us in shaping the future of the Calanais Visitor Centre and ensuring its legacy for generations to come.

Our Working Environment

At Calanais, every role matters. Whether you are welcoming visitors, serving coffee, preparing food, assisting in the shop or supporting behind the scenes, every member of our team contributes equally to the experience our visitors receive. We believe in treating everyone with the same respect, supporting one another, celebrating success together and creating a workplace where everyone feels valued.

Questions?

Interested?

If you'd like an informal conversation before applying, we'd be delighted to hear from you. Please get in touch with Heritage Manager Kathryn Lamont Smith at: kathryn@calanais.org

title: Experience Manager
description:
OVERVIEW

Experience a place of energy, passion, and excitement. A place where the joy of discovery and uncommon artistry blend to create exhilarating buying experiences—for true beauty enthusiasts. At Ulta Beauty, we’re transforming the world one shade, one lash, one cut at a time. Because beauty is powerful.

If you seek greater purpose—a place of vision, mission, and lived values—where voices are heard, contributions valued and recognized and growth opportunities abound, consider Ulta Beauty. Nowhere else are the possibilities quite this beautiful.

GENERAL SUMMARY & SCOPE

The Experience Manager (EM) is responsible for leading through Ulta Beauty’s mission, vision, and values in order to develop a high-performing team that consistently delivers top-line sales growth in retail and services. The EM leads a team of stylists, estheticians, guest coordinators (select locations), Assistant Services Managers (select stores), Sales Managers and boutique leads. This leader is accountable for all aspects of the guest experience, retail sales, and services businesses, including salon services, boutiques, retail sales, makeup, and guest satisfaction. The EM is accountable for Net Promoter Score (NPS) and delivering an exceptional guest experience. The EM drives their business through a focus on performance (NPS, services, boutiques, makeup, and retail sales), people (guest experience and associate culture), and process (operating procedures and compliance standards). This position requires a drive for results, a passion for the beauty industry, the ability to deliver exceptional guest service, and the ability to lead, influence, and develop their team.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES (*Essential Job Functions)

The EM is a champion of Ulta Beauty’s mission, vision, and values, and should demonstrate them skillfully and consistently by performing the following duties and responsibilities of the position (as well as all other projects/duties as assigned):

Performance

  • Promote a culture of accountability to meet or exceed the store’s goals related to services, boutiques, retail sales, guest loyalty (including credit), payroll, omni-channel, and retail shrink as set by Ulta Beauty for the store.
  • Drive company profitability through operational excellence, top-line sales growth and expense control.
  • Leverage store forecast and payroll budgets to support with store scheduling needs and communicate the needs to the GM to maximize productivity, achieve sales and payroll goals, and complete workload on time, and within the payroll budget.
  • Address underperforming metrics related to the store’s services, boutiques, retail sales, services sales, loyalty, store visit and audit results by developing strategies using company programs, tools, and resources to improve and grow these areas of the business.
  • Support direct reports in developing and maintaining their clientele.
  • Perform makeup applications, skincare analysis, and product demonstrations with guests to drive sales and guest service experience.
  • Take the initiative to stay informed regarding new and existing industry trends, products, and services during work time, and be knowledgeable about the ingredients and benefits of these trends, products, and services to better serve guests.
  • Maintain prompt, regular attendance as the EM and hold store associates accountable to the Ulta Beauty attendance policy.

People

  • Attract, hire, retain and source a diverse team of top talent for the salon and boutiques, leveraging a variety of methods including social media platforms, and efficiently address any staffing needs and open positions for the store.
  • Build a highly engaged team that embodies the Ulta Beauty brand through effective collaboration, open and honest two-way communication, prioritization of work and coaching to the behaviors that will drive guest loyalty.
  • Create an inclusive environment that inspires and encourages the growth and engagement of associates.
  • Support all aspects of manager and associate professional development, including training, providing individualized competency-based feedback and coaching, performance reviews, succession planning, and individual development plans to enable continuous development and drive sales performance.

title: Workflow Developer
description:
As a Workflow Developer at ITGoals, you will design and implement reliable, auditable enterprise workflows that automate user tasks, approvals, rejections, return/send-back actions, service-level rules, and end-to-end process status tracking for digital services. You will translate business processes into executable, maintainable workflow models, integrate with APIs and backend systems, and ensure resilience, observability, and production readiness in regulated environments.

  • Integrate workflows with REST APIs, backend services, external systems, and user-facing applications.

  • Document workflow models, integration points, decision rules, operational dependencies, and support procedures.

Required Experience

  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing workflow or BPM solutions in enterprise environments.

title: AI FDE - Enterprise Solutions
description:
We are looking for a True AI Forward Deployed Engineer (as coined by Palantir!) preferably with Supply Chain Domain Expertise. We are not looking for someone to run AI experiments. We are looking for someone to take AI all the way — from first conversation with a client to a system that runs in production and creates real business value. A

— 01 · THE OPPORTUNITY

AI leadership role.

Anthrobyte builds production-grade enterprise AI systems for global clients across Supply Chains & Enterprise Solutions. As we scale, we need an AI leader with Supply Chain Domain expertise who can hold the full journey: presales and discovery, solution design, consulting, and end-to-end development & deployment — all as one coherent capability.

This is less a traditional technical role and more a seat at the client table. You will work directly with the CTO, founding team, and enterprise clients to define how AI is scoped, architected, communicated, and delivered inside complex organisations. You will be the person who walks into a room with a messy problem and walks out with a solution the client believes in — and then makes it real.


FOUNDING ROLE

AI Lead / Supply Chain Expertise

Own the full AI engagement journey in Supply Chain — presales, solution design, consulting, and forward deployment — as one coherent capability.

GROWTH TRACK · MERIT-BASED

Principal AI & Solutions Lead

Grow into executive-level technical leadership — shaping company strategy, IP development, and client transformation at scale.



Requirements

— 02 · RESPONSIBILITIES

Own the solution. Drive it to production.

Presales & Solution Design

— Lead the pre-sales and technical discovery sessions with enterprise and mid-market clients globally — understand their pain points, data maturity, and AI readiness before anyone writes a line of code

— Own the solution design for AI proposals: use case scoping, high-level system design, data requirements, and ROI framing

— Build and present compelling PoC demos, solution blueprints, and technical proposals in partnership with the commercial team

— Respond to RFPs and RFIs with technically rigorous and commercially sharp responses that win confidence

Consulting & Client Engagement

— Act as a trusted AI advisor to client stakeholders — CXOs, VPs of Operations, IT leaders — not just a technical vendor on the call

— Run workshops, AI readiness assessments, and value stream mapping sessions at client sites and remotely

— Navigate ambiguous problem spaces and help clients articulate what they actually want to solve with AI, and why it matters

— Build long-term client relationships that translate into deepened engagements, referrals, and expanded mandates

Forward Deployment & Technical Delivery

— Be deeply involved in deployment — not just design. Understand production constraints, integration complexity, and change management realities

— Collaborate with engineering and data science teams to ensure solution designs are buildable and delivered to the quality clients expect

— Drive go-live milestones, client acceptance, and post-deployment success metrics with accountability

— Debug, iterate, and adapt: you own outcomes, not just deliverables. If something is broken, you fix it

Solution Design & Thought Leadership

— Define AI architecture patterns for the firm: LLM orchestration, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, multi-modal systems

— Stay ahead on applied AI research and emerging frameworks; bring relevant signals back to the team before the market does

— Mentor junior AI engineers and consultants on both client engagement craft and solution architecture rigour

— Contribute to Anthrobyte's knowledge capital — case studies, whitepapers, internal playbooks, and reusable solution accelerators

✶ The Growth Pathway

Demonstrate consistent excellence and the scope expands. You will grow into principal technical leadership — shaping company strategy, representing AI at investor and board conversations, building and leading a growing solutions team, and defining how AI transformation is delivered across every client engagement. This is not a title — it is a level of ownership that must be earned and continually re-earned.

— 03 · WHO YOU ARE

You operate across the full stack — from model architecture to client boardroom. You simplify complex problems without losing what makes them real, and you're as comfortable presenting to a VP of Supply Chain as you are reviewing a model eval report with a data science team.

You Bring

  • 5+ years of hands-on AI/ML experience (LLMs, NLP, computer vision, or advanced analytics) in production
  • Proven presales or solution consulting track record — you win client confidence with credibility
  • Strong storytelling: complex AI concepts made accessible to business audiences, without dumbing them down
  • Global client exposure (US, Europe, Middle East, or SEA) and cross-cultural fluency
  • Hands-on with Python, LLM frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, HuggingFace), and cloud AI (AWS, Azure, GCP)
  • Experience designing end-to-end AI systems: ingestion, pipelines, deployment, monitoring, and iteration
  • Comfort in ambiguity and 0→1 environments; startup or early-stage experience preferred

Bonus Signals

Supply Chain AI · Forward Deployment · Presales / SE · LLMs & RAG · MLOps · Global Clients · IIT / IIM / Tier-1 · B2B SaaS AI · Manufacturing / Logistics





Benefits

As per company norms

title: Accountmanager
description:

Je zal op technisch en regelgevend vlak volledig door ons opgeleid worden. Daarna ga je aan de slag met flexibele aanpasbare pakketten van alarmsystemen en camera’s. In belangrijke mate zal je zelf op zoek gaan naar commerciële opportuniteiten.

Wij zoeken een ras-verkoper met technische achtergrond. Maar met een ras-verkoper bedoelen we niet “de snelle jongen” die de handtekeningen jaagt maar de doordachte rustige, vastberaden persoon die doelbewust en vastberaden op zijn doel afgaat. Hierbij komen de volgende zaken o.a. aan bod:

title: AI Delivery Lead
description:
Anthrobyte wins by putting AI agents into the real operations of enterprise clients — and making them work, in production, where it matters. We need a leader who does this exceptionally themselves and builds a team that does it the same way. You'll own how we deliver AI, from the client's messy reality to a system they trust — and turn every engagement into repeatable capability inside our ATLAS platform.

This is a build-from-the-front role. You lead from inside the problem, not from a whiteboard.

What you'll own

— Embedded delivery. You go where the work is — inside the client's environment, alongside their operators — to understand their workflows, data, and constraints firsthand. You don't design in the abstract; you build against reality.

— End-to-end ownership. From business problem to architecture to a deployed, secured, monitored agent running in production and driving outcomes. You own the whole arc, not a slice of it.

— The product loop. You turn what you learn in the field into reusable patterns, accelerators, and standards inside ATLAS — so the next engagement is faster and we compound into a product, not a services treadmill.

— Building the team. This is the multiplier. You hire, mentor, and level up engineers to work the way you do — codifying your instinct into a playbook others can run. Success is a team who deliver like you, not you delivering everything.

— Client trust. You sit across from client security, data, and business leaders and earn their confidence — in architecture reviews, security reviews, and the room where decisions get made.


Requirements

What we're looking for

— Production track record. You've personally taken AI, ML, or agent systems into enterprise production — not demos, not pilots that died. You've worked with real client data and lived with what you shipped.

— Proof you build people. You've mentored engineers, set technical standards, and shaped how a team works. Evidence you can reproduce your skill in others, not just exercise it yourself.

— Range. You're equally comfortable writing code, whiteboarding architecture, and holding your own with a client's CISO.

— Systems mindset. You think in reliability and trust, not cleverness — enterprise AI is won on auditability and things that keep working.

— Ownership drive. You're energised by building something from early and shaping how it's done.

Bonus points

— Domain experience in supply chain, procurement, pricing, or other regulated / operational enterprise environments.

— Exposure to enterprise security, governance, and responsible-AI practices.

— A track record of growing engineers into strong, independent operators.

What this role is not

A back-office ML research lead. A pure people-manager who's left the tools behind. An architect who designs from a distance and never touches the client's reality. If you want to lead from a whiteboard rather than from inside the problem, this isn't it.

How we work

Small, high-trust, founder-close team. Governance-first, because our work runs inside clients' live operations. You'll have real authority over how we build and deliver — and the mandate to shape the team around strong talent.


How to apply

Tell us two stories. First: one AI system you took into enterprise production — the messy problem, how you built and secured it, and what broke along the way. Second: someone you made better — an engineer you grew, and how. Those two stories tell us more than any CV.

title: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology — Generalist, Customer-Facing
description:
Type: Full-time
Reports to: Founder, R&D Leader


Who we are

We build low-cost, high-reliability solutions to problems that usually demand expensive infrastructure — from forensic casework to diagnostic assays for cancer and rare diseases. We don't wait for the perfect answer or the bigger budget; we build with what's in the room, test it, and improve it together. If a problem looks unsolvable because nobody could afford to solve it properly, that's exactly the kind of problem we want.

Who we're looking for

A recent or soon-to-be MSc, MTech, or PhD graduate who'd rather bring a working idea to the table than wait for the "correct" one. You've spent time at the bench; you're comfortable with instrumentation, code, or spreadsheets; and you like figuring things out alongside other people rather than in isolation. You're not looking for a rulebook — you're looking for a hard problem and a team to solve it with. You want your work to reach real patients, real casework, real customers, not just a paper.

This is not a narrow role. You'll move between the bench, the systems that support it, and the people who depend on it working.

What you'll do

  • Develop and validate low-cost assays and lab workflows — spanning applications from forensic DNA casework to diagnostic tests for cancer and rare diseases — designed to work reliably outside well-resourced labs.
  • Build and troubleshoot the systems around the science: instrumentation, automation, data pipelines, and the practical engineering that makes a bench protocol into a repeatable product.
  • Work directly with customers and partners to understand their constraints, translate their problems into technical requirements, and support them through deployment and troubleshooting.
  • Operate with limited resources by design — you'll be expected to prototype with what's available, iterate fast, and find the cheaper, simpler path before reaching for the expensive one.
  • Take ownership across the full arc of a problem: from early bench experiments through to a working solution in a customer's hands.
  • Document rigorously enough that what you build can be trusted, repeated, and handed off — this is diagnostic and forensic work, where "it worked for me" isn't good enough.

Nice to have

  • Experience with diagnostic assay development, forensic genomics, or clinical/CLIA-adjacent workflows.
  • Familiarity with lab automation, instrument integration, or data/software tooling (Python, LIMS, or similar).
  • Startup or small-team experience where you had to do more than your job title suggested.

Why this role?

You'll work on problems that go straight from the bench to a person who needed the answer — a forensic case, a cancer diagnosis, a rare disease that finally gets identified. Small team, real stakes, and the freedom to build the solution your way when the standard playbook doesn't fit the budget.



Requirements

What you bring

  • MSc, MTech, or PhD in molecular biology, biomedical/genetic engineering, biotechnology, or a related field — or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • Real bench experience: molecular biology techniques (PCR, sequencing, extraction, assay development, or similar), not just coursework.
  • Comfort working across disciplines — willing to pick up systems/software/automation skills where needed rather than staying in one lane.
  • A track record of proposing and iterating on solutions rather than executing a fixed playbook — comfortable being wrong on the way to being useful.
  • Strong problem-solving instincts under real constraints: limited budget, limited equipment, limited time.
  • Genuine enjoyment of collaborative problem-solving: building on other people's half-formed ideas, and offering your own the same way.
  • Genuine interest in customer-facing work — explaining, listening, and adapting the solution to what the customer actually needs.

Show us how you think

Skip the cover letter. Instead, give us one example of a real problem you've solved recently — at the bench, in the field, in code, wherever. Be honest and try to limit problem-solving to fields in science, engineering, and technology. In 300 words or less, tell us:

  • What the problem was
  • How you solved it
  • If you had to solve it again today, what you would do differently?

We're not grading for polish — we're looking for how you actually approach a hard problem, and whether you're honest about what you'd change. Submissions over 300 words will not be reviewed.

Submit your application, including this example, via Biosecure ID's Careers Page:




Benefits

What we offer to candidates completing their probation period (3 months):
  • Equity: a real stake in what you help build, not just a paycheck.
  • Ownership from day one - you'll lead real projects, not shadow someone else's.
  • Support for your professional record: time and backing to publish papers, file patents, or co-author inventions that come out of your work here.
  • Room to build in the open — we encourage contributions to open-source tools, and we'll credit the people behind the work, not just the company.
  • A genuine learning budget — courses, certifications, conferences, whatever helps you get better at the problem in front of you.
  • Flexibility — flexible hours and hybrid/remote arrangements wherever the lab work allows it.
  • Honest, generous time off — and transparency about where the company stands, so trust isn't something we ask you to take on faith.
  • Health insurance — because good work shouldn't come at the cost of your health.
  • Proximity to impact — your work reaches an actual forensic case, an actual diagnosis and preventing future pandemics.

title: Consultant – Project Implementation of Combat Soil Salinity
description:
Organizational Setting

The Department of Nuclear Sciences and Applications implements the IAEA's Major Programme 2, "Nuclear Techniques for Development and Environmental Protection". This Major Programme comprises individual programmes on food and agriculture, human health, water resources, environment and radiation technologies. These programmes are supported by laboratories in Seibersdorf, Monaco and Vienna. The Major Programme's objective is to enhance the capacity of Member States to meet basic human needs and to assess and manage the marine and terrestrial environments through the use of nuclear and isotopic techniques in sustainable development programmes.

The Joint FAO/IAEA Centre of Nuclear Techniques in Food and Agriculture assists Member States of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the IAEA in using nuclear techniques and related technologies to improve food security, alleviate poverty and promote sustainable agriculture. The Joint Centre consists of five Sections, each with an associated laboratory (located in Seibersdorf, 45 km south-east of Vienna), in the areas of\: animal production and health; plant breeding and genetics; insect pest control; soil and water management and crop nutrition; and food safety and control.

The Soil and Water Management and Crop Nutrition Section and Laboratory assist Member States in developing improved soil and water management practices for sustainable intensification of agricultural production systems, the conservation of natural resources and the effective use of external inputs through applied and adaptive research and development activities, technology transfer and capacity building.



Main Purpose

To provide overall project management and technical expertise for the day-to-day activities for the Coordinated Research Project (CRP) on Developing Climate Smart Agricultural Practices to Combat Soil Salinity implemented by the Soil Water Management and Crop Nutrition (SWMCN) Subprogramme. The end result will be the timely implementation of CRP activities, coordination and organization of the regular meetings with the CRP partner and participants, and monitoring of the CRP progress.

Functions / Key Results Expected

  • Provide editorial review of all project reports from the CRP;

  • Provide technical input to project implementation, and monitoring of CRP progress in line with results-based management approaches;

  • Maintain a database and provide regular updates of the database for the experimental and analytical work across all countries, ensuring timely upload of data;

  • Develop and prepare success stories, brochures and guidelines for knowledge dissemination;

  • Communicate and coordinate regularly with CRP partner and participants to ensure timely delivery of project outputs

  • Provide technical expertise for meetings, renewal of CRP contracts, field procurement and transfer of consumables and equipment.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Soil and Water Management

Qualifications and Experience

  • Advanced university degree (masters) in agricultural sciences, soil science, environmental sciences or related disciplines.

  • Minimum five years of work experience in one or more of the following areas\:

    • Experience in project management and project budgeting specifically within the UN System;

    • Experience in database management;

    • Experience in capacity-building measures in program/project implementation;

    • Project Management qualification and experience (desired);

    • Clear communication skills (written and verbal) in English;

    • Experience in liaising with key stakeholders and key relationship management;

    • Experience in project progress reporting;

    • Experience in developing brochures and guidelines for knowledge dissemination;

    • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Adobe suite.

title: Firmware Engineer
description:
OB DESCRIPTION

Firmware Engineer

Embedded Systems and Linux

Location:

New Delhi

Employment Type:

Full-time

Experience Level:

2-4 Years

Department:

Engineering / Firmware

Role Purpose

The engineer will convert product and system requirements into reliable firmware that interfaces correctly with electronic hardware, sensors, communication modules, actuators, and higher-level applications. The position requires practical ownership from architecture and driver development through integration, debugging, verification, release, and field support.

Key Responsibilities

  • Microcontroller firmware: Develop and maintain bare-metal or RTOS-based firmware for AVR, STM32, and ESP32 devices using C and C++.

  • Python development: Develop Python tools and utilities for test automation, build support, telemetry and log analysis, calibration, simulation, manufacturing, and system integration.

  • Robotics integration: Integrate embedded firmware with sensors, encoders, actuators, motor controllers, safety interlocks, and higher-level robotic software, including ROS or ROS 2 interfaces where applicable.

  • Embedded Linux: Configure cross-compilation toolchains, build applications and system components, integrate board support packages, and troubleshoot software on embedded Linux computers.

  • Yocto development: Create and maintain Yocto layers, recipes, image configurations, machine settings, package selections, and reproducible builds for target hardware.

  • ArduPilot customization: Understand the ArduPilot codebase, modify firmware for product-specific behavior, integrate sensors or peripherals, configure boards, and validate changes through bench and flight-oriented testing.

  • ESP32 development: Build connected firmware using ESP-IDF or an equivalent framework, including peripheral control, communication, networking, logging, update, and fault-recovery functions.

  • Drivers and board support: Develop and integrate low-level drivers, hardware abstraction layers, startup code, interrupt handling, timers, DMA, memory interfaces, and board configuration.

  • System communication: Implement and debug UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, USB, Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, MAVLink, and other product-specific protocols.

  • Firmware reliability: Design watchdog handling, error detection, safe-state behavior, configuration storage, bootloaders, firmware update mechanisms, and recovery paths appropriate to the product.

  • Verification and debugging: Create unit, integration, bench, and hardware-in-the-loop tests; diagnose timing, memory, concurrency, communication, and hardware-interface faults using suitable tools.

  • Release management: Maintain source control, build instructions, configuration records, change history, release notes, traceable binaries, and technical documentation.

  • Cross-functional support: Work with hardware, systems, controls, testing, manufacturing, and field teams to define interfaces, review risks, reproduce issues, and deliver corrective updates.

Core Technical Areas

Area

Expected Knowledge and Application

Languages

Strong embedded C and practical C++ knowledge, plus Python for automation, test tools, build support, simulation, telemetry processing, and log analysis.

Microcontrollers

AVR, STM32, and ESP32 architecture, clocks, GPIO, interrupts, timers, ADC, PWM, DMA, nonvolatile memory, low-power modes, and vendor SDKs.

Real time software

Task design, scheduling, synchronization, queues, timing, interrupt interaction, resource sharing, and debugging in an RTOS such as FreeRTOS.

Embedded Linux

Cross-compilation, Linux processes and services, permissions, filesystems, networking, shell tools, system logs, device access, and deployment to target systems.

Yocto Linux

BitBake, recipes, layers, images, packages, machine configuration, SDK generation, build reproducibility, and integration of custom applications.

Autopilot and robotics

ArduPilot architecture, MAVLink, sensors, actuators, simulation and logging, together with robotic interfaces, motor controllers, safety interlocks, and ROS or ROS 2 integration awareness.

Hardware interfaces

Schematic and datasheet interpretation, peripheral bring-up, protocol timing, electrical constraints, driver behavior, and cooperation with hardware engineers.

Debug and test

GDB, JTAG or SWD, serial logs, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, static analysis, unit tests, integration tests, and repeatable fault reproduction.



Requirements

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or diploma in Electronics, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Embedded Systems, or a closely related discipline.

  • Demonstrated experience developing production firmware for microcontrollers, including at least one STM32 or ESP32 platform and practical familiarity with AVR devices.

  • Strong programming ability in embedded C, working knowledge of C++ for constrained or real-time systems, and practical Python experience for automation, testing, build tooling, simulation, or data and log analysis.

  • Experience with embedded Linux cross-compilation and with configuring or maintaining Yocto-based software images.

  • Ability to read schematics and component datasheets, debug firmware at the boundary between software and hardware, and integrate robotic sensors, encoders, actuators, or motor controllers.

  • Experience using Git, structured code review, reproducible build procedures, issue tracking, and documented firmware releases.

  • Ability to investigate complex faults systematically and communicate findings through clear code, test evidence, and technical documentation.

Preferred Experience

  • Direct modification of ArduPilot firmware, including custom board support, sensor or actuator integration, MAVLink changes, parameter handling, or vehicle-specific behavior.

  • Use of ArduPilot simulation, software-in-the-loop testing, hardware-in-the-loop testing, flight logs, and controlled field-validation procedures.

  • Linux board support work involving U-Boot, device trees, kernel configuration, kernel modules, systemd services, or custom root filesystems.

  • Bootloader design, secure boot, signed firmware, over-the-air or field updates, rollback, and recovery mechanisms.

  • Experience with DroneCAN, CANopen, Ethernet-based protocols, GNSS receivers, inertial sensors, radio modules, motor controllers, or payload interfaces.

  • Familiarity with ROS 2 or micro-ROS, PX4 or another autopilot stack, robotic simulation tools, shell scripting, continuous integration, static analysis, and automated test equipment.

  • Firmware development for defence, aerospace, robotics, industrial control, automotive, or other reliability-sensitive systems.

Adhere to information security policies, protect the confidentiality of organizational data, and promptly report suspected security incidents or vulnerabilities to the responsible team.

title: AI ML Architect / Senior FDE Lead
description:
We are looking for a True AI Forward Deployed Engineer (as coined by Palantir!) who can architect enterprise-grade AI systems, not just prototype them. We are not looking for someone to hand off a design doc and walk away. We are looking for someone to take AI all the way — from system architecture to production infrastructure that scales with the client’s business.


01 · THE OPPORTUNITY

A senior technical leadership role at the intersection of architecture rigor, hands-on engineering, and production-grade delivery.

Anthrobyte builds production-grade enterprise AI systems for global clients across industries. As we build out our presence in the U.S. from San Francisco, we need a senior AI/ML architect who can hold the full technical journey: system architecture, agentic and LLM infrastructure design, hands-on build, and production deployment — all as one coherent capability.

This is not a role where you hand off an architecture diagram and move on to the next project. You will work directly with the CTO, founding team, and enterprise clients to define how AI systems are architected, engineered, and hardened for production inside complex organisations. You will be the person who walks into a room with a messy, high-stakes technical problem and walks out with an architecture the team can actually build — and then builds it.

CURRENT ROLE

AI ML Architect & Senior FDE Lead

Own the full technical journey of AI engagements — architecture, hands-on build, forward deployment, and production hardening — as one coherent capability.

GROWTH TRACK · MERIT-BASED

Principal AI Architect

Grow into executive-level technical leadership — shaping the company’s AI architecture standards, technical IP, and engineering practice at scale.



Requirements

02 · RESPONSIBILITIES

Own the architecture. Ship it to production.

Architecture & Solution Design

· Lead architecture discovery with enterprise clients — assess data maturity, system landscape, and AI readiness before a single line of code is written

· Own end-to-end system design for AI proposals: model selection, RAG/agentic architecture, data pipeline design, infrastructure sizing, and ROI framing

· Build working prototypes, architecture blueprints, and technical proof points that de-risk the engagement before full build

· Set technical standards and reusable architecture patterns that the broader engineering team builds on

Forward Deployment & Production Engineering

· Be hands-on in the build — write production code, design data pipelines, and stand up the infrastructure your architecture calls for

· Own deployment realities: integration complexity, security and compliance constraints, scaling, and observability

· Drive go-live milestones, uptime, and post-deployment performance with direct accountability for outcomes

· Debug, iterate, and adapt in production — when something breaks, you own the fix, not just the postmortem

Technical Leadership & Client Engagement

· Act as the trusted technical authority to client stakeholders — CTOs, VPs of Engineering, platform teams — not just a vendor on the call

· Translate deep technical tradeoffs into language business stakeholders can act on, without losing the substance

· Collaborate with presales and delivery teams to ensure every commitment made to a client is technically buildable

· Build long-term technical trust with clients that turns single engagements into expanded, multi-year mandates

Platform & Applied AI Research

· Define AI architecture patterns for the firm: LLM orchestration, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, and evaluation frameworks

· Stay ahead of applied AI research and emerging frameworks; bring what matters back to the team before it’s common knowledge

· Mentor AI engineers on both architecture rigor and forward-deployed delivery craft

· Contribute to Anthrobyte's technical knowledge capital — architecture playbooks, reusable accelerators, and internal tooling

THE GROWTH PATHWAY

Demonstrate consistent excellence and the scope expands. You will grow into principal technical leadership — shaping the company’s AI architecture strategy, representing engineering at investor and board conversations, building and leading a growing engineering team, and defining the technical standard for every client engagement. This is not a title — it is a level of ownership that must be earned and continually re-earned.


03 · WHO YOU ARE

You operate across the full stack — from distributed systems design to client boardroom. You simplify complex architectures without losing what makes them robust, and you're as comfortable in a production incident channel as you are presenting system design to a VP of Engineering.

You Bring

· 8+ years of hands-on AI/ML and software architecture experience, with production systems at real scale

· Proven track record architecting and shipping LLM-based or agentic AI systems into production — not just PoCs

· Deep hands-on fluency: Python, distributed systems, LLM frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, HuggingFace), and cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP)

· Experience designing end-to-end AI/ML platforms: data pipelines, model serving, evaluation, and monitoring

· Strong client-facing communication — able to defend architecture decisions to both engineers and executives

· Comfort operating in ambiguity and 0→1 environments; startup or forward-deployed experience strongly preferred

· A bias toward ownership — you close loops without being asked, and you treat production issues as yours to fix

title: Pipeline for short assignments - Consultant (Legal) - Nuclear Law
description:
This is a re-opening of the pipeline. Previously submitted applications are still under consideration.

Contract Type and Duration

Consultancies for expert missions and assignments, typically with duration 3-15 days.

Organizational Setting

The Office of Legal Affairs (OLA), which reports directly to the Director General, provides legal services of the highest standard to the Director General, the Secretariat, and the policy making organs of the IAEA, as well as to Member States, in connection with the implementation of the IAEA’s activities.

The Nuclear and Treaty Law Section of OLA provides legal advice and support in the areas of nuclear safety, nuclear security, civil liability for nuclear damage, nuclear energy, nuclear applications, and technical cooperation. The Section is responsible for implementing the IAEA Legislative Assistance Programme and for carrying out the IAEA’s depositary functions. It provides advice and training to Member States on legal instruments adopted by or under the auspices of the IAEA and on national legislation for the safe, secure, and peaceful uses of nuclear technology.

Main Purpose

Under the guidance of the Head of the Nuclear and Treaty Law Section, the consultant contributes specialized legal expertise in international and national nuclear law and related legal frameworks including, legislative, regulatory and contractual aspects relevant to the safe, secure, and peaceful uses of nuclear technology.

The consultant may participate in IAEA missions and other activities addressing these frameworks. The consultant may review draft and enacted legislation and contribute to awareness-raising missions, workshops and training courses, including through the delivery of lectures, case studies, and practical exercises designed to transfer legal knowledge and skills.

Qualified consultants who are available for short-term and/or temporary assignments are invited to register and create their Candidate Profile.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

Candidates must have expertise in at least one of the following areas\:

-International legal instruments adopted by and under IAEA auspices on nuclear safety, nuclear security, and civil liability for nuclear damage.

-Legal frameworks for the safe, secure and peaceful uses of nuclear technology and its applications.

-Drafting legislation in all areas of nuclear law and reviewing draft and enacted nuclear legislation covering one or more of the following\:

national systems of regulatory control of nuclear facilities and activities,

radiation protection,

radiation safety,

decommissioning of facilities,

emergency preparedness and response,

mining and processing of radioactive material,

transport of radioactive material,

radioactive waste and spent fuel management,

nuclear liability,

nuclear security including physical protection of nuclear material and facilities and/or the security or radioactive sources.

-Advising on legislation and related aspects concerning nuclear power programmes and projects, including one or more of the following subjects\:

Environmental protection,

EPR,

Occupational health and safety of workers,

Protection of intellectual property,

Local land use controls,

Foreign investment,

Taxation, fees, electricity tariffs and incentives,

Roles of national and local governments,

Stakeholders and public involvement,

International trade and customs,

Financial guarantees and any other required financial legislation including R&D.

-Advising on commercial and contractual arrangements for nuclear projects.

-Knowledge of key IAEA publications, safety standards, nuclear security guidance and other guidance documents including the IAEA Milestones Approach.

Education, Experience and Language Skills

Member of a national bar or equivalent. Proven ability to prepare legal drafts and advise a broad range of stakeholders from governmental bodies. Minimum of ten years relevant experience, including several years at the international level and/or advising governmental officials on nuclear related matters.

Excellent command of written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of another other UN official language (i.e. Arabic, Chinese, French, Spanish and/or Russian) is an asset.

Remuneration

The remuneration for consultant assignments depends on the assignment and the consultant’s qualifications and ranges between €300 and €480 per day. In case duty travel is required within the assignment, a daily subsistence allowance (DSA) and travel costs are provided. Health coverage and pension fund are the responsibility of the incumbent.

Further details on the duration, duty station, organizational context and qualification requirements may and will be provided to one or more preselected consultants for a specific assignment at the discretion of IAEA responsible staff.

Applications from qualified women and candidates from developing countries are encouraged.

The Pipeline will be used to create a roster of consultants. The validity of the roster application will be for two years upon the submission of the application. Registration in the Pipeline does not constitute any formal obligation on the side of the IAEA to offer any type of employment. Updates will only be provided to candidates who are being considered for opportunities.

Applicants should be aware that IAEA staff members are international civil servants and may not accept instructions from any other authority. The IAEA is committed to applying the highest ethical standards in carrying out its mandate. As part of the United Nations common system, the IAEA subscribes to the following core ethical standards (or values)\: Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for diversity. Staff members may be assigned to any location. The IAEA retains the discretion not to make any appointment to this vacancy, to make an appointment at a lower grade or with a different contract type, or to make an appointment with a modified job description or for shorter duration than indicated above. Testing may be part of the recruitment process.
