title: Senior System and Bsuiness Analyst / Product Owner
description:
We are seeking a Senior System Analyst who will also act as a Product Owner for one of our digital products. This role is primarily focused on system analysis, system design, and professional requirements documentation, including System Requirements Specifications (SRS) and Business / Product Requirements Documents (BRD/PRD).

In parallel, the role will carry select Product Owner responsibilities, ensuring the assigned digital product delivers business value while remaining technically sound, scalable, and well-documented. The successful candidate will serve as a key bridge between business, product, and engineering, translating product vision and business needs into clear, structured, and UML-driven system specifications.

Key Responsibilities:

System Analysis & Design (Primary Focus)

  • Lead requirements elicitation, analysis, and validation for digital systems and products.

  • Produce and maintain high-quality SRS, BRD, and PRD in accordance with industry standards.

  • Translate business and product needs into clear, testable functional and non-functional system requirements.

  • Design and document system behavior using UML (use case, sequence, activity, and component diagrams) and BPMN.

  • Perform gap analysis, impact analysis, and system improvement assessments.

  • Ensure requirements traceability across the SDLC and alignment with architecture, integration, and security standards.

Product Owner Responsibilities

  • Act as Product Owner for an assigned digital product, owning feature definition and requirement clarity.

  • Define and prioritize product features, epics, and user stories based on business value and system constraints.

  • Maintain and refine the product backlog in collaboration with stakeholders and development teams.

  • Define acceptance criteria and support UAT to ensure product and system requirements are met.

Requirements

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or a related discipline

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience as a Senior System Analyst or Business Analyst, with demonstrated responsibility for end-to-end requirements management

  • Proven experience supporting or acting as a Product Owner for a digital product or system.

System Analysis & Documentation Expertise

  • Advanced expertise in producing professional System Requirements Specifications (SRS) aligned with industry and IEEE standards

  • Strong experience in developing and maintaining Business Requirements Documents (BRD) and Product Requirements Documents (PRD)

  • Ability to translate business and product needs into clear, structured, testable functional and non-functional requirements

  • Strong command of requirements traceability, version control, and change management

System Design & Modeling Skills

  • Deep understanding of system analysis methodologies and SDLC frameworks (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid)

  • Proven proficiency in UML and BPMN, including:

  • Use Case Diagrams

  • Sequence Diagrams

  • Activity Diagrams

  • Component / High-Level Architecture Diagrams

  • Experience performing gap analysis, impact analysis, and system design assessments

Product Owner & Delivery Capabilities

  • Practical experience defining product features, epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria

  • Ability to manage and prioritize a product backlog while considering system dependencies and technical constraints

  • Experience supporting UAT planning and execution to validate system and product requirements

Technical & Integration Knowledge

  • Strong conceptual knowledge of database design, data models, and system data flows

Tools & Collaboration

title: System Engineer (Lab)  — Generalist, Customer-Facing
description:
Type: Full-time
Reports to: Founder, R&D Leader


Who we're looking for

A recent or soon-to-be MSc, MTech, or PhD graduate who'd rather bring a working idea to the table than wait for the "correct" one. You've spent time at the bench, you're comfortable with instrumentation, code, or a spreadsheet, and you like figuring things out alongside other people rather than in isolation. You're not looking for a rulebook — you're looking for a hard problem and a team to solve it with. You want your work to reach real patients, real casework, real customers, not just a paper.

This is not a narrow role. You'll move between the bench, the systems that support it, and the people who depend on it working.

What you'll do

  • Develop and validate low-cost assays and lab workflows — spanning applications from forensic DNA casework to diagnostic tests for cancer and rare diseases — designed to work reliably outside well-resourced labs.
  • Build and troubleshoot the systems around the science: instrumentation, robotics, automation, data pipelines, and the practical engineering that makes a bench protocol into a repeatable product.
  • Design, build, and maintain robotic and automated systems — liquid handlers, custom rigs, sensor-driven workflows — including autonomous systems that can sense, decide, and act with minimal human intervention.
  • Work directly with customers and partners to understand their constraints, translate their problems into technical requirements, and support them through deployment and troubleshooting.
  • Operate with limited resources by design — you'll be expected to prototype with what's available, iterate fast, and find the cheaper, simpler path before reaching for the expensive one.
  • Take ownership across the full arc of a problem: from early bench experiments through to a working solution in a customer's hands.
  • Document rigorously enough that what you build can be trusted, repeated, and handed off — this is diagnostic and forensic work, where "it worked for me" isn't good enough.

Nice to have

  • Experience with diagnostic assay development, forensic genomics, or clinical/CLIA-adjacent workflows.
  • Experience building autonomous or semi-autonomous systems — closed-loop control, sensor fusion, or decision-making pipelines.
  • Contributions to open-source projects (lab automation, robotics, or bioinformatics tooling especially relevant).
  • Startup or small-team experience where you had to do more than your job title suggested.

Why this role?

You'll work on problems that go straight from the bench to a person who needed the answer — a forensic case, a cancer diagnosis, a rare disease that finally gets identified. Small team, real stakes, and the freedom to build the solution your way when the standard playbook doesn't fit the budget.



Requirements

What you bring

  • MSc, MTech, or PhD in molecular biology, biomedical/genetic engineering, robotics, mechatronics, biotechnology, or a related field — or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • Real bench experience: molecular biology techniques (PCR, sequencing, extraction, assay development, or similar), not just coursework.
  • Hands-on experience with lab robotics and automation — liquid handling systems, custom hardware rigs, or sensor/actuator-driven workflows.
  • Working knowledge of Python (the standard for lab automation —Hamilton Venus and Tecan EVO, SiLA2-style device integrations, LIMS/data pipelines); C/C++ for firmware or hardware control is a strong plus; exposure to ROS (Robot Operating System) is a plus if you've built or contributed to autonomous systems.
  • Comfort working across disciplines — willing to pick up systems/software/robotics skills where needed rather than staying in one lane.
  • Familiarity with open-source development practices and an active GitHub presence — we want to see how you build, not just hear about it.
  • A track record of proposing and iterating on solutions rather than executing a fixed playbook — comfortable being wrong on the way to being useful.
  • Strong problem-solving instincts under real constraints: limited budget, limited equipment, limited time.
  • Genuine enjoyment of collaborative problem-solving: building on other people's half-formed ideas, and offering your own the same way.
  • Genuine interest in customer-facing work — explaining, listening, and adapting the solution to what the customer actually needs.

Show us how you think

Skip the cover letter. Instead, give us one example of a real problem you've solved recently — at the bench, in the field, in code, wherever. In 300 words or less, tell us:

  • What the problem was
  • How you solved it
  • If you had to solve it again today, what you would do differently.

We're not grading for polish — we're looking for how you actually approach a hard problem, and whether you're honest about what you'd change. Submissions over 300 words will not be reviewed.

Submit your application, including this example on




Benefits

What we offer to candidates completing their probation period (3 months):
  • Equity: a real stake in what you help build, not just a paycheck.
  • Ownership from day one - you'll lead real projects, not shadow someone else's.
  • Support for your professional record: time and backing to publish papers, file patents, or co-author inventions that come out of your work here.
  • Room to build in the open — we encourage contributions to open-source tools, and we'll credit the people behind the work, not just the company.
  • A genuine learning budget — courses, certifications, conferences, whatever helps you get better at the problem in front of you.
  • Flexibility — flexible hours and hybrid/remote arrangements wherever the lab work allows it.
  • Honest, generous time off — and transparency about where the company stands, so trust isn't something we ask you to take on faith.
  • Health insurance — because good work shouldn't come at the cost of your health.
  • Proximity to impact — your work reaches an actual forensic case, an actual diagnosis and preventing future pandemics.

title: Physical AI Engineer
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Physical AI Engineer

Edge AI, Autonomy and Simulation

Location:

New Delhi

Employment Type:

Full Time

Experience Level:

3+ Years

Department:

Engineering / AI and Autonomy

Role Purpose

The engineer will turn research and system requirements into perception and autonomy software that performs reliably on real hardware. The position requires practical ownership from data collection and model development through onboard optimization, integration with drone software, simulation, and controlled hardware testing.

Key Responsibilities

● Vision models: Develop, train, fine tune, and evaluate YOLO based object detection and tracking pipelines for drone imagery and video.

● Data and evaluation: Build labeling, augmentation, dataset versioning, error analysis, and repeatable evaluation workflows across lighting, motion, altitude, and environmental conditions.

● Model optimization: Apply quantization, pruning, model conversion, and runtime profiling to meet latency, memory, compute, power, and thermal limits on target hardware.

● Reinforcement learning: Design training environments, reward functions, observations, actions, constraints, and evaluation procedures for autonomous behavior.

● Maneuver algorithms: Develop and test planning, guidance, obstacle avoidance, trajectory generation, and control support algorithms for complex maneuvers within defined safety limits.

● Embedded deployment: Package inference services and supporting software for embedded computers, including Yocto recipes, dependencies, startup, logging, configuration, and updates.

● System integration: Connect perception and autonomy modules with sensors, camera streams, telemetry, navigation estimates, autopilot interfaces, and ground tools.

● Simulation and testing: Set up realistic scenarios, run software in the loop and hardware in the loop tests, inject faults and edge cases, and compare simulated performance with recorded or physical tests.

● Software delivery: Write maintainable Python and C++ code, review changes, automate tests and builds, document design decisions, and produce reproducible releases.

● Cross functional support: Work with firmware, hardware, controls, and simulation engineers to define interfaces, review risks, reproduce issues, and support controlled field trials.

Core Technical Areas

Area

Expected Knowledge and Application

Computer vision

YOLO training and inference, detection metrics, tracking, camera geometry, preprocessing, image quality, and failure analysis.

Machine learning

PyTorch or a comparable framework, dataset management, experiment tracking, generalization checks, and reproducible training.

Edge optimization

INT8 or mixed precision quantization, calibration, operator support, model export, profiling, and accuracy versus latency tradeoffs.

Reinforcement learning

Policies, environments, reward design, exploration, constraints, offline evaluation, and transfer from simulation to hardware.

Autonomy algorithms

State estimation inputs, path and trajectory planning, collision avoidance, maneuver constraints, guidance logic, and autopilot integration.

Embedded Linux

Yocto recipes and images, cross compilation, services, containers or packages where appropriate, device access, logs, and deployment.

Simulation and test

Scenario design, sensor and dynamics models, software in the loop, hardware in the loop, regression tests, telemetry replay, and performance measurement.

Software engineering

Python and C++, Git, code review, unit and integration tests, CI, clear interfaces, observability, and release documentation.



Requirements

Required Qualifications

● Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in Computer Science, Electronics, Robotics, Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related discipline.

● At least 3 years of hands on experience developing and evaluating computer vision or autonomy software, including a YOLO family detector deployed to embedded hardware.

● Practical knowledge of quantization and runtime profiling, with evidence of measuring model accuracy, latency, memory use, and hardware resource limits.

● Experience developing algorithms for robotic or drone autonomy and testing them in simulation.

● Working knowledge of reinforcement learning concepts and the ability to define meaningful training and evaluation setups.

● Strong Python skills, working C++ skills, and experience integrating software on embedded Linux, including Yocto based builds.

● Ability to debug across models, software, sensors, system timing, and onboard hardware using logs and repeatable tests.

Preferred Experience

● Experience with ArduPilot or PX4, MAVLink, ROS 2, camera and IMU data, GNSS, and telemetry pipelines.

● Deployment with ONNX, TensorRT, OpenVINO, TFLite, or hardware specific inference runtimes and accelerators.

● Synthetic data generation, domain randomization, visual simulation, and methods for reducing the gap between simulation and field performance.

● Development of software in the loop or hardware in the loop test benches, automated scenario suites, and telemetry replay tools.

● Experience with real time constraints, fault handling, safe behavior when perception is uncertain, and controlled field validation.

● AI or autonomy development for defence, aerospace, robotics, industrial automation, or other reliability sensitive systems.

title: Global Technical Coordinator — Major Projects Delivery (MPD)
description:
Global Technical Coordinator — Major Projects Delivery (MPD)

1. Role Objective

The Global Technical Coordinator coordinates the deployment, standardisation, and sustained adoption of InEight across regions, deploying wherever programme priorities and implementation demand require. Serving as the primary coordination link among business stakeholders, project delivery and project controls teams, Regional SMEs, technical resources, and global programme leadership, the role supports the complete implementation lifecycle\: from readiness assessment, process definition, and configuration through to training, Go-Live, stabilisation, and transition to business-as-usual operations.

The Global Technical Coordinator translates global MPD delivery standards and regional requirements into practical, repeatable processes that can be applied consistently across business units, offices, projects, and geographies. The role is a hands-on implementation and business process role that leads the development and maintenance of project delivery standards — including handbooks, SOPs, work instructions, process maps, RACIs, user guides, training materials, governance models, and reporting standards — in each implementation context. The role requires comfort operating across different regions, cultures, time zones, business sectors, and organisational levels, adapting implementation support to local needs while maintaining alignment with global programme standards.

The GTC operates under the direction of the Global Implementation Lead, who owns the deployment lifecycle and to whom the GTC reports and escalates on all implementation matters. The GTC coordinates with the Global Technical Lead on platform standards and quality gate requirements, but does not report to or escalate directly to the GTL independently of the GIL.

2. Key Responsibilities

2.1 Implementation Coordination

• Coordinate InEight implementations across regions as programme needs require, executing plans issued by the Global Implementation Lead in alignment with the global MPD roadmap.

• Coordinate business units, project teams, Regional SMEs, Project Managers, Project Controllers, and technical resources throughout readiness, onboarding, configuration, training, Go-Live, stabilisation, and transition to business-as-usual support.

• Lead implementation planning and governance, facilitating workshops and status meetings while managing milestones, deliverables, resources, dependencies, decisions, risks, issues, and competing priorities.

• Monitor and communicate implementation performance, ensuring regional and project requirements remain aligned with global standards, governance, and platform expectations while supporting multiple projects across countries, time zones, languages, and business sectors.

2.2 Process Standardisation & Documentation

• Lead the development and governance of InEight operating standards, translating project delivery and project controls requirements into practical, repeatable, and auditable processes aligned with global programme expectations.

• Develop and maintain controlled documentation including Project Controls handbooks, SOPs, work instructions, user guides, process maps, RACIs, implementation playbooks, training materials, checklists, templates, and governance frameworks.

• Coordinate stakeholders and facilitate process workshops to assess current-state practices, define future-state processes, establish roles, controls, approvals, decision rights, systems, records, and KPIs, and eliminate unnecessary complexity, duplication, variation, and manual workarounds.

• Manage the implementation documentation lifecycle and continuous improvement process, maintaining approved materials in a centralised repository with appropriate ownership, version control, review cycles, and lessons learned, while promoting consistent reuse across regions, business units, and projects.

2.3 Configuration and Workflow Support

• Translate approved business processes and standards into InEight configuration requirements, coordinating pre-configuration reviews to confirm scope, data, roles, approvals, dependencies, and key business decisions.

• Coordinate Regional SMEs, project teams, and technical resources during configuration, ensuring that workflow decisions align with approved operating processes and global platform standards.

• Manage configuration governance and quality assurance, documenting decisions, assumptions, dependencies, and approved variations, escalating deviations or unnecessary customisation to the Global Implementation Lead for review and resolution.

• Coordinate workflow validation and implementation readiness, including business reviews, user acceptance testing, defect resolution, acceptance, and alignment among configuration, procedures, training, and reporting, incorporating lessons learned into configuration standards.

2.4 Project Controls & Business Process Support

• Integrate Project Controls practices into InEight workflows, applying knowledge of cost, budget, forecasting, schedule, progress measurement, change, document control, and project reporting processes.

• Coordinate Project Controls and project delivery stakeholders to standardise definitions, data structures, process steps, controls, calendars, governance checkpoints, and reporting requirements while maintaining global consistency.

• Improve processes, systems, and data integration by reducing manual effort and duplicate entry, clarifying system responsibilities, data ownership, process hand-offs, and sources of truth across InEight and related enterprise platforms.

2.8 Data, Reporting & Digital Support

Significant concerns are escalated by the GIL to the Global Technical Lead, Global Business Owner, Regional Business Owners, or appropriate governance forums.

title: Solicitor - Property Litigation

title: Cyber Security Engineer
description:

title: Senior Odoo Implementation Consultant (Hybrid — Project-Based)

Data, testing and go-live

Training and handover

- Strong experience with Odoo Website and eCommerce

- Hands-on experience with : branches, staging, deployments and backups

- Proven ability to write BRDs, workflow diagrams, functional specifications and test scripts

- Proven experience with large data migrations

- Excellent Arabic and English, written and spoken

- Able and willing to travel for project work, inside and outside Egypt

Strong advantages

- Retail, wholesale (B2B), real estate, construction, or multi-branch implementations

- Experience with payment gateways (Moyasar, Tap, HyperPay, PayTabs, Tamara, Tabby) or carriers (SMSA, Aramex)

- Live projects with Subscriptions, Appointments, Helpdesk, or Marketing Automation

- Technical understanding: Python, the Odoo ORM, XML views, QWeb, OWL and PostgreSQL

- Experience with major-version upgrades

- Pre-sales experience: demos and solution presentations

- Project management experience

What we offer

- A project fee agreed upfront and paid by milestone

- Hybrid flexibility, with a structured delivery process and a senior team

APPLICATION CONDITIONS — READ BEFORE APPLYING

How to apply

Apply through Wuzzuf and include:

title: Senior HSE Engineer
description:
1) Compliance & Governance

  • Ensure adherence to Egyptian laws and regulations (e.g., environmental permits, hazardous substances, civil defense/fire codes, labor law) and local authority/site licensing requirements.

  • Maintain and improve ISO 45001 (OHSMS) and ISO 14001 (EMS) management systems; lead internal audits, corrective actions, and surveillance/recertification preparations.

  • Develop, review, and roll out HSE policies, procedures, SOPs, and permit‑to‑work systems across all retail sites.

2) Risk Management & Process Safety (Retail Focus)

  • Conduct and update risk assessments (HIRA/JSA), bow‑ties, and job safety analyses for fueling, tanker offloading, tank gauging, confined space entry, hot works, and working at height.

  • Lead process safety controls for storage tanks, piping, dispensers, vapor recovery, pressure relief, and electrical bonding/earthing; verify integrity through inspections and testing.

  • Implement and monitor contractor HSE requirements (pre‑qualification, onboarding, method statements, tool‑box talks, supervision).

3) Site Assurance & Inspections

  • Plan and perform station audits/inspections (housekeeping, ATEX/EX equipment, emergency equipment, signage, spill kits, firefighting systems, separators).

  • Track actions to closure; report trends and recommend engineering and behavioral controls.

  • Verify tanker fleet compliance (ADR-equivalent practices, driver competence, defensive driving, spill prevention).

4) Incident Prevention, Reporting & Learning

  • Lead incident/near‑miss investigations using root cause techniques (5‑Why, ICAM, TapRooT® style), issue reports, and drive corrective/preventive actions.

  • Champion HSE reporting pyramid/iceberg concepts to boost near‑miss, hazard observation, and unsafe condition reporting and learning (REX).

  • Manage statutory emergency response arrangements, drills, and coordination with local authorities and Civil Defense.

5) Training, Culture & Engagement

  • Deliver and track HSE training (induction, PTW, LOTO, confined space, working at height, spill response, fire warden, manual handling).

  • Coach site managers/dealers and supervisors on behavior-based safety, leadership walkdowns, and toolbox talks.

  • Lead campaigns (heat stress, driving safety, slips/trips/falls) and Safety Days.

6) Environment & Sustainability

  • Oversee spill prevention and response, waste management, water/oil separator maintenance, and air emissions (vapor recovery).

  • Monitor utilities, fuel losses, and product variance; support leak detection, tank tightness testing, and remediation.

  • Track environmental KPIs and statutory reporting; support sustainability initiatives (energy efficiency, solar, EV/CNG expansion).

7) Data, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Maintain HSE dashboards (LTIFR, TRIR, near‑miss rate, audit closure rate, training completion).

  • Present monthly HSE reports to management; recommend risk‑based investments and CAPEX for safety improvements.

  • Digitize HSE workflows (inspection checklists, incident reporting, action tracking) where possible.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Petroleum, or HSE).

  • 5–7+ years of progressive HSE experience, with at least 3–5 years in petroleum retail/fuel depots/CNG/LPG or equivalent high‑risk operations.

  • Certifications: NEBOSH IGC (minimum); ISO 45001 Lead Auditor and/or ISO 14001 Lead Auditor preferred; OSHA/IOSH an advantage.

  • Demonstrated experience with incident investigations, risk assessments, contractor HSE, and emergency response.

  • Strong knowledge of Egyptian regulatory requirements and international best practices (NFPA/API/IECEx/ATEX concepts applicable to retail).

  • Fluent English; strong report writing and presentation skills.

  • Willingness to travel nationwide (40–60%).

title: Pipeline for Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Materials Professionals and Experts-Short-Term Consultancy
description:
This is a re-advertisement, please note that applicants who have already submitted their application do not need to resubmit an application. All existing applications are still under consideration.

Organizational Setting

The Division of Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Waste Technology (NEFW) comprises the Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Materials Section, the Waste Technology Section, the Decommissioning & Environmental Remediation Section and the Research Reactor Section. The Division seeks to support Member States in building their capacity to access technologies, to share good practices and to develop safe and effective approaches across all aspects of research reactors, nuclear fuel cycle, decommissioning, radioactive waste management and environmental remediation.

The Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Materials Section (NFCMS) assists interested Member States in the development of safe, environmentally friendly, economically viable, proliferation-resistant and sustainable fuel cycle options and it encourages information exchange on the exploration, mining and processing of uranium and thorium, on the design, manufacturing and performance of nuclear fuels, on the management of spent fuel, and on the development of advanced and innovative nuclear fuels and fuel cycles.

Main Purpose

In order to provide qualified candidates to IAEA Departments for multiple short-term positions and assignments, the Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Materials Section in the Division of Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Waste Technology keeps a roster of Interested applicants. Qualified consultants and experts worldwide who are available for short-term and/or temporary assignments are encouraged to register and create their profiles. If you are interested in working at the IAEA and fulfil the requirements to work within the Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Materials Section in any of the fields listed below, please complete an online application.

Registration into the Pipeline does not constitute in any form a commitment on the part of the IAEA for taking a particular application into consideration in the recruitment process for any vacancy. Pipeline registration is only valid for 2 years. Candidates need to re-register again after two years of initial date of registration to be considered as an active pipeline applicant.

The main purpose of the experts’ involvement will contribute to the Section’s aim to foster technology and knowledge transfer, the adoption of sound policies and strategies, and promotes information exchange, with the aim of building Member States' capacity in all aspects of the nuclear fuel cycle.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • perform technical editing of multi-author documents;
  • develop training courses building on existing guidance/reference material and lectures;

  • develop a sequence of web articles based on existing publications and documents.

Depending on the specific assignment, the expected adequate level of expertise ranges from basic general understanding to prior professional experience with some in-depth technical understanding in\:

  • Expertise|Nuclear Engineering|Nuclear Raw Material;
  • Expertise|Nuclear Chemical Engineering;

  • Expertise|Nuclear Engineering|Irradiation Effects on Equipment and Materials;
  • Expertise|Nuclear Engineering|Nuclear Engineering and Technology;

  • Expertise|Nuclear Engineering|Management Systems for Nuclear Facilities;

  • Expertise|Nuclear Engineering|Fuel Cycle and Waste Management;
  • Expertise|Nuclear Engineering;
  • Expertise|Nuclear Safety|Design Basis Accident Analysis and Methods;
  • Expertise|Radiation, Transport and Waste Safety|Radioactive Waste and Spent Fuel Management.

Education, Experience and Language Skills

  • University Degree or Advanced University Degree in Geology, Chemistry, Mineral Resources, Economic Geology, Mining, Material Science, Nuclear Fuel, Nuclear Engineering, or related fields.
  • Doctorate Degree is an asset.
  • At least 3 years of relevant experience in editing, document writing and/or training and knowledge transfer in the expert areas of the nuclear fuel cycle (from uranium/thorium resources exploration and production to spent fuel management through nuclear fuel design, fabrication and operation, and nuclear fuel cycle facilities operation).

Arni Medica Private Limited is an ISO 13485:2016 and ISO 9001:2015 certified medical device and in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) manufacturer based at the Medical Devices Park, Sangareddy (Hyderabad), Telangana. title: Internship Coordinator (part-time)
description:
INTERESTED APPLICANTS SHOULD SEND RESUME & COVER LETTER TO HR@CyclesofChange.org


Position Overview

The Internship Coordinator (IC) is a part-time position that coordinates and supports Cycles of Change’s youth internship programs, providing young people with opportunities to deepen their knowledge and skills in bicycle mechanics, bicycle and public transit navigation, leadership, and community bike shop operations.

The IC works closely with Bike Club Coordinators, Bike Club Educators, and the Operations Generalist to recruit and support youth participants, develop curriculum, coordinate program logistics, maintain participant relationships, and ensure program outcomes and reporting requirements are met. The IC will report to the Operations Generalist.

Internship programs include opportunities for participants to explore bike mechanics, navigate the Bay Area by bicycle and public transit, and learn about the role of community bike shops such as the Bikery. Two makeup sessions will be scheduled for each program series as needed.

Hourly Rate: $30.73/hour

This role is budgeted to work within the range of 8-12 hours a week, with opportunity for more depending on need and seasonal availability.

Program Areas

School-Year Internship — August–May

  • Two youth participants per semester.

  • Approximately 25 hours per participant over 10 sessions (2.5 hours per session), or an equivalent schedule.

    • Up to two additional makeup weeks may be scheduled as needed.

Winter Bike Build — December

  • Lead a community bike-building project during winter break.

  • Four youth participants will support the preparation of bicycles for a holiday bike giveaway.

  • Programmatic hours: two 4-hour programs per week for two weeks (December 20 - January 2)

  • 1 additional staff member will support IC for twice a week for 2 weeks (1 week prior to the build and the 2 weeks of the build)


Summer Internship — May–July

  • Four youth participants per summer.

  • Approximately 25 hours per participant over 10 sessions (2.5 hours per session), or an equivalent schedule.

  • 1 additional staff member will support the IC during all sessions and for 1 week prior to the internship’s start.

Youth Outcomes

The Internship Coordinator will support programs designed to achieve the following outcomes:

Youth Leadership & Development

  • At least 85% of youth participants will report experiencing at least one meaningful leadership opportunity during the program.

Knowledge Acquisition & Skill Development

  • At least 85% of participants will report learning new skills related to bicycles, including navigation, bicycle mechanics, and basic bicycle repair.

Staffing & Supervision Responsibilities

  • Coordinate staffing needs for internship programs and projects requiring additional staff support.

  • Identify potential Cycles of Change staff members in collaboration with Bike Club Coordinators.

  • Interview, onboard, and train support staff as needed for internship programming.

  • Provide clear expectations and guidance to staff supporting internship participants.

Communication & Relationships

As a member of the Cycles of Change staff, the Internship Coordinator is expected to:

  • Respond to internal and external communications within 48–72 hours.

  • Establish and maintain positive, supportive relationships with youth participants that foster a learning environment and empower youth to engage with opportunities available through Cycles of Change.

  • Collaborate with Bike Club Educators and Coordinators to create a smooth transition for eligible Bike Club participants into internship programs.

  • Work closely with Bike Club Coordinators and the Operations Generalist to coordinate programming and participant support.

Curriculum Development

  • Develop and maintain curriculum for semester-based internship programming.

  • Adapt curriculum and activities to meet the needs, interests, and skill levels of participating youth.

  • Incorporate opportunities for bicycle mechanics, navigation, leadership, and community bike shop learning.

Recruitment & Collaboration

  • Coordinate youth recruitment for each internship program in collaboration with the Bike Club/Afterschool Coordinator.

  • Support outreach and communication with potential participants.

  • Coordinate participant transitions from Bike Club and other Cycles of Change programs into internship opportunities.

Budget & Financial Management

  • Manage the OFCY internship budget in coordination with the Operations Generalist.

  • Monitor program expenses and allocate resources in ways that prioritize youth experience and program outcomes.

  • Communicate anticipated financial needs and budget concerns in a timely manner.

Data & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate daily attendance records for all internship participants.

  • Create and administer pre- and post-program participant surveys.

  • Collect and maintain required program data.

  • Collaborate with the Operations Generalist on data collection, reporting, and evaluation.

  • Submit required program data and reports at least two weeks prior to applicable deadlines.

Facilities & Operations

  • Maintain key access and follow facility procedures for assigned Cycles of Change spaces.

  • Follow all space-use expectations outlined in applicable MOUs.

  • Support safe, organized, and welcoming program spaces for youth participants.

Collaboration

The Internship Coordinator works closely with:

  • Bike Club Coordinators

  • Bike Club Educators

  • Operations Generalist

  • Additional program staff and support staff

  • Youth participants and, as appropriate, their families and school/community partners

title: Domain Architect
description:
Job Title: Domain Architect Automation & Integration

Location: Chennai Department: Technology Excellence Reporting To: CTO – Technology Excellence

Works Closely With: Director – Strategic Initiatives & Programs (SIP), Director – Service Delivery, AI Program Manager, Platform Engineering, Infrastructure Teams, Security/Compliance

---

Job Purpose:

The Domain Architect Automation & Integration is responsible for defining and governing architecture standards, reference patterns, and integration approaches within the automation domain across UiPath execution environments, ERP/workflow platforms (Odoo/BR Connect), and API-driven integrations.

The role provides system-level design guidance to ensure automation solutions are scalable, modular, interoperable, secure, audit-ready, and cost-effective across multiple clients and heterogeneous EMR/PMS environments. The Architect drives consistency through pragmatic standards and reusable frameworks, and partners with delivery teams, platform engineering, security, and operations to reduce risk and improve speed of execution.

This is a platform architecture and technical leadership role (not a primary “build every bot” role).

---

Key Responsibilities:

1. Automation Domain Architecture

1. Define target-state automation domain architecture and integration patterns across UiPath, ERP/workflow systems, and API integrations.

2. Establish and maintain architectural standards, reusable templates, reference frameworks, and modular design principles (e.g., configuration, exception taxonomy, logging schema).

3. Define centralized observability standards (logging, metrics, traceability, alerts) and ensure automation telemetry supports operational and audit requirements.

4. Define architecture review checkpoints, quality gates, and lifecycle standards for automations (intake assessment design build test release monitoring), in alignment with the broader delivery governance model.

5. Publish and maintain Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) and reference designs to reduce ambiguity and prevent “snowflake” implementations.

---

2. Workflow & ERP Integration


1. Architect deep integration patterns between automation platforms and Odoo (BR Connect) to enable workflow-native automation.

2. Define event-driven triggers and workflow patterns (e.g., status transitions, queues, webhooks, scheduled triggers) that scale across clients and departments.

3. Ensure alignment between business process intent and technical implementation by translating process goals into system workflows, data contracts, and automation patterns.

4. Standardize integration mechanisms between internal systems and external platforms (EMR/PMS, payer portals, clearinghouse interfaces), including data validation and error recovery patterns.

---

3. Orchestration & Control Strategy

1. Define reference orchestration approaches (UiPath Orchestrator / hybrid / custom control plane) and guardrails, aligned to operational constraints and platform direction.

2. Establish workload distribution standards across execution environments (server pools, VM/terminal servers, cloud access constraints), including queue strategy and priority rules.

3. Define capacity planning standards (robot concurrency, scheduling windows, SLA-based throughput) and partner with operations/engineering to implement scalable execution models as demand grows.

4. Define the automation performance tracking and SLA monitoring framework (availability, success rate, throughput, MTTR) and align reporting/escalation processes with operations and support teams.

5. Provide architectural input to licensing and cost-scaling decisions (capacity triggers, utilization signals, ROI assumptions) to support delivery without creating bottlenecks.

---

4. API & System Integration Governance

1. Design and review RESTful integrations and integration contracts (schemas, idempotency, retry strategy, error codes, versioning).

2. Promote an API-first integration strategy and reduce fragile UI automation where APIs or data interfaces are feasible.

3. Architect secure authentication and authorization patterns (OAuth2, token handling, secrets rotation), including credential vault integration and least-privilege access.

4. Ensure interoperability across EMR, ERP/workflow, automation platforms, and external systems with audit-ready traceability and controlled data flows.

---

5. Python & Service Framework Oversight


1. Provide architectural guidance for Python-based automation services (e.g., OCR/document processing, data transformation utilities, integration services), ensuring clear interfaces, operational readiness, maintainability, and measurable quality targets.

2. Establish standards for logging, exception handling, monitoring, deployment, scaling, and secure configuration management for services.

3. Ensure service-oriented design principles are followed (separation of concerns, clear APIs, versioning, resilience, testing strategy).

---

6. AI-assisted Automation & Intelligent Workflows

1. Define how AI-assisted automation can be introduced safely through concrete patterns (human-in-the-loop approvals, confidence thresholds, fallbacks, audit logs) and clear integration boundaries between AI services and automation workflows.

2. Establish reusable workflow primitives/components (classification, routing, triage, exception enrichment) that can be adopted consistently across use cases.

3. Partner with the AI team to define governance patterns for AI-assisted automation (confidence thresholds, human-in-the-loop approvals, monitoring, prompt/version control where applicable).

4. Enable adoption of AI-assisted automation enhancements aligned with measurable business outcomes (TAT, accuracy, denials reduction, productivity) in partnership with delivery and operations teams.

---

7. Technical Leadership & Governance

1. Facilitate architecture design reviews, technical decision forums, and cross-team alignment (RPA, BA, Internal Platform, IT/Infrastructure, Operations).

2. Define and drive adoption of automation domain best practices and solution design standards (coding standards, review checklists, release readiness criteria) while keeping governance lightweight and enabling delivery speed.

3. Mentor UiPath and Python teams through enablement (templates, reference implementations, review checklists, coaching).

4. Collaborate with Infrastructure and Security teams to ensure environments meet compliance/security requirements (PHI/PII, access control, logging policies, retention).

5. Partner with leadership to translate automation domain goals into phased reference architectures and adoption plans with measurable outcomes and risk management.

6. Clarify role boundaries and build team autonomy: architect enables and governs—delivery teams execute.

---

Skills and Competencies:

1. Strong system-level thinking with ability to design scalable, modular, secure, and operable automation domain architectures.

2. Deep understanding of automation platforms and integration patterns (queues, orchestration, event-driven workflows, APIs).

3. Strong knowledge of UiPath (Studio, Orchestrator concepts, REFramework, best practices, exception handling, logging).

4. Working knowledge of Python-based services and API integration patterns; able to review designs and guide engineering standards (hands-on development is a plus).

5. Experience integrating ERP/workflow platforms (Odoo preferred) and designing workflow-driven automations.

6. Strong understanding of REST API design, interoperability, and reliability patterns (idempotency, retries, versioning).

7. Knowledge of orchestration strategies and distributed execution models (UiPath Orchestrator concepts preferred).

8. Strong security mindset: secrets management, credential vault integration, least privilege, audit logging, compliance-aligned access controls.

9. Excellent documentation and architectural modeling capability (reference architectures, ADRs, runbooks).

10. Strong problem-solving skills with ability to prioritize pragmatic solutions over over-engineering.

11. Strong communication skills with both technical teams and business stakeholders.

12. Ability to challenge legacy patterns constructively and drive adoption through enablement, not micromanagement.

---

Qualifications:

1. 7-10+ years of experience in automation architecture, system integration, platform engineering, or similar roles (or equivalent demonstrated capability).

2. Minimum 3+ years hands-on experience in UiPath automation (architecture/design, governance, and best practices).

3. Experience with Python and API-based integrations (ability to collaborate with service engineers, review designs, and ensure operability/security).

4. Experience working with ERP/workflow platforms (Odoo preferred) and cross-system integration.

5. Exposure to orchestration platforms and distributed system design (UiPath Orchestrator or equivalent concepts).

6. Experience in healthcare/RCM domain is an advantage (PHI/PII handling, audit readiness, client IT coordination).

7. UiPath certifications and/or Cloud/Integration certifications are preferred.

---

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

1. Architecture Adoption & Quality Rate: % of automation initiatives aligned with defined standards and passing architecture review checkpoints.

2. Reusability Index: Adoption rate and measurable impact of reusable components/templates (reduced build time, reduced defects).

3. Integration Stability: Reduction in integration-related incidents; improved reliability of API and workflow integrations.

4. Scalability & Capacity Governance: Demonstrated ability to scale workloads within defined SLA windows using capacity planning and orchestration strategy.

5. Governance Effectiveness: Timeliness and quality of architecture artifacts (ADRs, reference patterns, roadmaps) without creating delivery bottlenecks.

6. Innovation Enablement: Delivery of phased enhancements aligned with automation domain priorities (e.g., orchestration adoption, AI-assisted patterns) with measurable business outcomes.

title: Senior Software Testing Engineer
description:
We are looking for a Software Testing Engineer with at least 4 years of hands-on experience in software testing to join our team.

The ideal candidate should have a strong understanding of the software testing lifecycle and be able to analyze requirements, prepare test scenarios and test cases, execute different testing cycles, report defects clearly, and contribute to improving overall product quality.

Key Responsibilities

  • Analyze and understand business and functional requirements.

  • Design, document, and execute test scenarios and test cases.

  • Perform Manual Testing, including Functional, Regression, Integration, Smoke, Sanity, and End-to-End testing.

  • Work with project and testing documentation such as BRD, FRD, Test Plans, Test Cases, Test Reports, and UAT documents.

  • Perform API Testing using tools such as Postman, Swagger, or similar tools.

  • Validate API requests, responses, status codes, authentication, and business flows.

  • Have hands-on experience in Test Automation using Playwright.

  • Be able to build and maintain reusable automation scripts for regression and end-to-end scenarios.

  • Have experience with Performance Testing using tools such as Apache JMeter and/or Locust.

  • Understand concepts such as Load Testing, Stress Testing, Spike Testing, and performance result analysis.

  • Have good knowledge of SQL and database validation.

  • Experience with MySQL is preferred.

  • Be able to identify, reproduce, document, and track defects with clear steps, expected results, actual results, and supporting evidence.

  • Experience using Jira or similar bug-tracking tools is preferred.

  • Experience with test-management tools such as Xray, TestRail, Zephyr, or similar tools is a plus.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.

  • Minimum of 4 year of experience in software testing.

  • Experience using Generative AI or AI-assisted testing/development tools such as ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Claude, or similar technologies.

  • Experience using AI for test case generation, automation support, requirement analysis, documentation, or defect investigation.

  • Basic understanding of CI/CD pipelines and Git is an advantage.

  • Good analytical, communication, documentation, and problem-solving skills.

  • Leadership skills and customer interface

We are looking for someone who is not only able to execute predefined test cases, but can also understand the business flow, identify risks, design effective test coverage, automate critical scenarios, validate APIs and databases, and contribute to the overall quality of the solution.

title: BDM – Medical Disposables (OEM/Private-Label)
description:
Job Title: Business Development Manager – Medical Disposables (OEM / Private-Label)
Location: Major metro base (pan-India and export travel)
Department: Business Development – Disposables
Experience: 5–10 years (medical disposables / OEM contract-manufacturing BD)
Employment Type: Full-time, on-site

About Arni Medica
Arni Medica Private Limited is an ISO 13485:2016 and ISO 9001:2015 certified medical device and in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) manufacturer based at the Medical Devices Park, Sangareddy (Hyderabad), Telangana. We design and manufacture nephrology, infusion therapy, respiratory care and surgical disposables, and are building a full IVD diagnostics franchise spanning clinical chemistry, electrolyte/ISE, blood gas (ABG), fluorescence immunoassay (FIA) and chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) platforms — backed by Class 100K/10K cleanrooms, EtO sterilization and a CDSCO manufacturing licence (MFG/MD/2023/000942).

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop new customers and OEM / private-label / contract-manufacturing opportunities for medical disposables.
  • Build and manage distributor, super-stockist, C&F and stockist networks; drive primary and secondary sales across territories.
  • Manage RFQ / quotation, costing & margin negotiation, MOQ, sampling and validation cycles for OEM accounts.
  • Coordinate with operations and quality on supply commitments, ISO 13485 compliance and delivery timelines.
  • Participate in exhibitions, customer meetings and institutional / tender business development.
  • Track targets, collections, credit-period and market intelligence.

Desired Candidate Profile

  • Education: Graduate in Science, Pharmacy or Engineering; MBA preferred.
  • Experience: 5–10 years in medical disposables / surgical consumables sales or OEM / contract-manufacturing business development.


Technical Skills & Keywords
Medical disposables sales, OEM / private-label / contract manufacturing, B2B / institutional selling, distributor appointment, super-stockist & C&F management, primary & secondary sales, RFQ / quotation, costing & margin negotiation, MOQ, GeM / tenders, collections, ISO 13485 product familiarity (IV cannula, infusion sets, blood tubing, dialysis & surgical consumables).

Preferred / Good to Have

  • Existing OEM client book and export exposure.
  • Strong institutional selling and channel-management track record.
  • Import-export awareness (Incoterms, documentation).

What We Offer

  • Modern, ISO 13485 / CDSCO-compliant manufacturing environment with cleanroom infrastructure.
  • Direct collaboration with R&D, Regulatory and senior leadership — visible impact, fast decisions.
  • Competitive compensation, commensurate with experience (negotiable; as per industry standards).
  • Accelerated career growth in a fast-scaling, export-oriented MedTech company.

How to Apply


Email your CV to jobs@arnimedica.com with the position title in the subject line.

title: Finance & Accounts Manager
description:
Role Overview

The Finance Manager shall be responsible for managing the overall Finance and Accounting function of Alpha Plus Technologies (APT). This role oversees Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Financial Reporting, Statutory Compliance, Budgeting, and Financial Governance of the organization.

The Finance Manager will lead the Finance team, ensuring smooth day-to-day financial operations while maintaining financial discipline across the organization.

This role reports (for interim period) directly to the CEO and requires a highly dependable professional capable of independently managing the finance function, ensuring statutory compliance, supporting audits, and enabling effective financial planning and decision-making.


Roles & Responsibilities

1. Financial Management & Governance

· Take ownership of the entire Finance & Accounting function of the organization.

· Ensure accurate maintenance of books of accounts and financial records in accounting systems.

· Supervise and review accounting entries related to payments, receipts, invoices, taxes, and reimbursements.

· Provide financial insights and advisory support to the CEO and/or Board for strategic decision-making.

2. Accounts Receivable & Client Billing Management

· Oversee preparation and dispatch of client renewal quotes and invoices within defined timelines.

· Ensure timely payment follow-ups and resolution of long-outstanding receivables.

· Monitor reconciliation of payments received vs receivables.

· Ensure proper tracking of TDS deductions and reconciliation with Form 26AS.

3. Accounts Payable & Vendor Payment Management

· Review and approve vendor invoices, service provider bills, and utility payments.

· Ensure timely vendor payments and verification of tax applicability including TDS.

· Oversee reconciliation of corporate credit cards and expense documentation.

· Maintain vendor records including bank details and statutory information.

4. Statutory Compliance & Taxation

· Ensure timely filing of statutory returns including GST, TDS, PF, Professional Tax, and other compliances.

· Review GST returns (GSTR‑1, GSTR‑3B) and ensure reconciliation of GSTR‑2A.

· Ensure preparation and filing of quarterly TDS returns and reconciliation with statutory records.

· Coordinate with Company Secretary and Chartered Accountants for statutory filings.

5. Financial Reporting & MIS

· Prepare and review monthly financial and management reports.

· Provide periodic financial updates to the CEO regarding financial performance and compliance.

· Ensure accuracy of financial trackers, reconciliation statements, and documentation.

6. Budgeting & Financial Planning

· Prepare and manage organizational budgets in consultation with the CEO and/or Finance Advisor.

· Monitor budget vs actual expenditure and highlight variances.

· Provide financial forecasts and cost-control recommendations.

7. Audit & Regulatory Coordination

· Coordinate with statutory auditors for half‑yearly and annual audits.

· Ensure readiness of financial records, reconciliation statements, and supporting documentation.

· Support responses to statutory notices or financial scrutiny matters.

8. Banking & Financial Liaison

· Liaise with banks for corporate banking matters including accounts, credit facilities, and guarantees.

· Ensure timely renewal and closure of bank guarantees.

· Maintain relationships with financial institutions and advisors.

9. Team Leadership & Operational Oversight

· Lead and supervise the Finance team.

· Ensure adherence to SOPs and financial processes.

· Review team outputs and drive operational improvements.

· Coordinate effectively with internal departments.

10. Decision Making & Ownership

· Act as the primary finance decision-maker for operational finance matters.

· Identify financial risks and implement corrective actions.

· Drive continuous improvement in financial processes, controls, and reporting systems.

11. ISO Compliance & Governance

· Define and implement Quality Management System (QMS) and Information Security Management System (ISMS) processes for product management, ensuring compliance with ISO standards.

· Maintain documentation for ISO audits and oversee corrective actions to address any non-compliance.

· Collaborate with internal and external auditors to ensure smooth execution of ISO-compliant processes.

· Drive a culture of quality and security by reinforcing ISO principles across product management workflows.



Requirements

Qualification / Skill-sets

  • Graduates / Professional Degree-holders / Post Graduates desirous of a Management and Leadership career in Finance & Accounting.
  • Chartered Accountant (CA) / Inter CA completed. Full CA qualification preferred.
  • 10+ years of experience in Finance, Accounting, and Financial Management roles.
  • 3+ years of experience in Management roles.​
  • Strong knowledge of Accounting Standards, GST, TDS, and statutory compliances.
  • Key Skills:

o Hands‑on experience managing complete accounting functions including receivables, payables, taxation, financial reporting, budgeting, and audit coordination.

Roles & Responsibilities

  • Set up, start up, operate and shut down injection molding machines (hydraulic, electric and hybrid) and auxiliary equipment: material dryers, hopper loaders, granulators, mold temperature controllers, chillers and sprue pickers/robots.

title: Revenue Assurance Officer
description:
A. Sales revenue verification

1. Verify every unit reported as sold meets the qualifying criteria before it enters the weekly or monthly sales report.

2. Match each SPA to the approved price list; flag any price below list or discount outside the Delegation of Authority.

3. Confirm buyer KYC and AML/CFT checks are on file, including source-of-funds for cash or high-value payments.

4. Check that each sale is recorded in the ERP/CRM against the correct unit, buyer, price and payment plan, and that no unit is sold twice.

5. Review cancellations, resales, swaps and transfers for approval, forfeiture calculation and correct reversal of revenue.

6. Flag sales recorded in the wrong month or not yet qualifying to Finance for correction.

B. Sales collection verification

1. Reconcile the PDC register to each payment plan: every instalment has a cheque or agreed payment method, with correct amount and date.

2. Match collections to bank statements monthly; investigate unmatched receipts, cash receipts and receipts in third-party names.

3. Track bounced cheques, replacements and legal notices; confirm penalties and late fees are applied or properly waived.

4. Track receivables ageing by project and unit; escalate balances past agreed thresholds.

5. Confirm no unit is handed over or title transferred before full payment or an approved exception.

C. Leasing revenue verification

1. Verify each lease is signed, registered with the relevant authority, and matches the approved rate card and leasing policy.

2. Check rent-free periods, discounts and incentives against approval limits.

3. Reconcile three sources for every unit: physical occupancy on site, ERP status and the lease register. Flag occupied-but-not-billed, billed-but-vacant and expired-but-occupied units.

4. Confirm renewals are processed and repriced before expiry, and that expired contracts are either renewed, vacated or escalated.

5. Verify service charges, utilities recharges, parking and other ancillary income are billed completely.

D. Leasing collection verification

1. Reconcile security deposits and rent PDCs held to the lease register and to the cheque custody log.

2. Match rent receipts to bank statements; investigate cash collections and unallocated receipts.

3. Age tenant arrears; confirm follow-up, notices and legal escalation follow policy.

4. Verify deposit refunds on exit: deductions supported by the move-out inspection, refunds approved and paid to the tenant of record.

E. Commissions, incentives and payouts

1. Verify every commission payment advice against verified sales and leases before disbursement.

2. Check commission tier, agent attribution and splits; watch for units clubbed under other agents' names to reach a higher tier.

3. Confirm broker and external agent fees are contracted, approved and paid only after qualifying collection.

F. ERP data integrity and reporting

1. Maintain the Sales Verification Register and a Lease Verification Register as the single tracked record of exceptions.

2. Reconcile sales and leasing reports to the ERP and to Finance's ledger each month.

3. Recommend report templates and system fields that close gaps, for example missing PDC status or fee columns.

4. Raise ERP status corrections with Property Management and Sales and confirm they are made.

G. Controls, policy and compliance

1. Test compliance with the leasing policy, sales policy and Delegation of Authority.

2. Cover the relevant items in the real estate compliance program (RERA and related regulations) and AML/CFT requirements for property transactions.

3. Document control gaps found during testing and suggest practical fixes.

4. Report red flags and suspected fraud to the Head of GRC immediately.

H. Stakeholder management and follow-up

1. Agree findings with process owners before reporting, with evidence attached.

2. Track every open exception to closure in the audit follow-up tracker.

3. Support walkthroughs for Sales, Leasing and PM teams when policies or controls change.



Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance or Commerce.

• 4 to 6 years in accounts receivable, credit control, audit, or real estate sales or leasing administration.

• Basic understanding of how property sales and leases work: reservations, payment plans, PDCs, lease contracts, deposits.

• Real estate experience in Qatar or the GCC.

• Professional qualification (ACCA, CIA or CMA) will be an added advantage.

Competencies:

  • An ability to work independently and as a member of a team in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

Qualifications:

  • 3+ years’ experience in a R&D/QC Analyst role.

Testing, Commissioning & Fault Resolution

  • Analysing traces and test results to identify and resolve issues.

  • Producing clear, accurate test reports and as-built documentation.

  • Performing proactive and reactive maintenance on live and new-build networks.

  • Diagnosing and repairing faults to minimise downtime.

  • Replacing components and ensuring long-term network reliability.

Health, Safety & Compliance

  • Maintaining PPE and equipment to a high standard.

  • Participating in the Emergency Response Support rota when required.

Site Operations & Quality

  • Reporting progress and issues through digital systems.

title: RF Engineer
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

RF Engineer

Signal Processing, FPGA and RF Localization

Location:

New Delhi

Employment Type:

Full Time

Experience Level:

3+ Years

Department:

Engineering / RF and Signal Processing

Role Purpose

The engineer will turn RF sensing requirements into a working multi receiver system that detects and localizes RF sources using time difference of arrival (TDOA). The position requires practical ownership from signal chain design and receiver synchronization through low latency DSP, FPGA firmware, source position estimation, and verification through laboratory and field measurements.

Key Responsibilities

● SDR system design: Select and configure SDR platforms, RF front ends, sampling rates, bandwidths, gain settings, filtering, and I/Q capture paths for the required signals.

● Digital signal processing: Develop detection, filtering, channelization, resampling, correlation, spectral analysis, and signal quality estimation algorithms.

● Receiver synchronization: Align distributed receivers with suitable frequency and time references; characterize clock drift, timestamp uncertainty, calibration offsets, and transport delay.

● TDOA localization: Estimate time differences from captured signals, resolve ambiguous correlations, solve for source position, and report confidence and geometry related limits.

● Real time processing: Build efficient streaming pipelines for high rate I/Q data with controlled buffering, loss detection, latency, memory use, and CPU or accelerator load.

● FPGA firmware: Develop and validate FPGA logic for SDR data paths, including sample capture, timestamping, digital downconversion, filtering, decimation, DMA, and host interfaces.

● System integration: Connect receivers, FPGA logic, host software, networking, timing sources, storage, visualization, and control interfaces into a reliable sensing system.

● Test and calibration: Create repeatable tests using signal generators, known transmitters, recorded I/Q data, simulation, and field measurements; compare estimates with ground truth.

● Engineering delivery: Maintain schematics and interface assumptions, code and HDL reviews, versioned builds, performance reports, calibration records, and release documentation.

● Cross functional support: Work with RF hardware, embedded software, FPGA, and field test teams to trace errors across the complete signal and timing path.



Requirements

Core Technical Areas

Area

Expected Knowledge and Application

RF fundamentals

Receiver noise figure, dynamic range, gain, filters, antennas, interference, propagation, multipath, and practical spectrum measurement.

DSP

Complex sampling, Fourier analysis, filtering, decimation, detection thresholds, cross correlation, spectral estimation, and fixed point effects.

SDR platforms

RF transceiver configuration, I/Q streaming, sample formats, clocking, calibration, driver APIs, and recorded data replay.

Timing and sync

Shared references or disciplined clocks, PPS or equivalent timing, timestamp alignment, drift compensation, and error budget analysis.

TDOA estimation

Correlation peak selection, wideband delay estimation, outlier rejection, sensor geometry, multilateration, uncertainty, and performance under multipath.

FPGA development

Verilog, VHDL, or SystemVerilog; pipelined DSP, timing closure, clock domain crossing, memory use, AXI or equivalent buses, and simulation.

Real time software

C++ or C for low latency pipelines, Python for analysis and tooling, concurrency, backpressure, profiling, and stable data interfaces.

Verification

Signal generators, oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, logic analyzers, FPGA test benches, I/Q datasets, and ground truth field tests.

Required Qualifications

● Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in Electronics, Telecommunications, Electrical Engineering, Signal Processing, Computer Engineering, or a closely related discipline.

● At least 3 years of hands on experience with SDR hardware and development of DSP algorithms for sampled RF signals.

● Experience designing or implementing real time I/Q data acquisition and processing under bandwidth, latency, and compute constraints.

● FPGA development experience, including HDL design, simulation, hardware debugging, and timing closure for streaming data paths.

● Understanding of time synchronization and its effect on TDOA estimation and RF source localization.

● Strong C or C++ programming ability, practical Python for analysis and test automation, and disciplined use of Git and technical documentation.

● Ability to diagnose system errors across RF hardware, clocks, FPGA logic, software, networking, and measurement setup.

Preferred Experience

● Development of multi receiver TDOA, multilateration, direction finding, spectrum monitoring, or passive RF sensing systems.

● Use of GNU Radio, UHD, SoapySDR, or vendor SDR SDKs; familiarity with Linux device interfaces and embedded deployment.

● DSP implementation on FPGA or SoC platforms, including digital downconversion, high throughput DMA, fixed point optimization, and hardware software partitioning.

● Experience with GNSS disciplined oscillators, PPS timing, PTP or other network time methods, and distributed sensor calibration.

● Statistical estimation, tracking, confidence metrics, sensor fusion, or robust localization in multipath and low signal to noise conditions.

● Deployment of distributed RF systems in field conditions, including reliable networking, remote diagnostics, and repeatable calibration procedures.

title: Full-Stack Engineer (Django & Next.js)

Parents discover, book and pay for kids' activities, classes, camps, attractions and days out, and venues and tour operators sell through us. The product includes a consumer app and website, a merchant portal for venues, an aﬃliate portal, subscriptions and loyalty, and a large operational admin used daily by our team. The platform has been in production for years and handles real payments, multi-currency pricing, three languages (English, Arabic, Russian), geospatial search and live inventory from partner APIs.

We are a small, senior team based in the UAE, and we build with AI: coding agents such as Claude Code are our daily tools, and AI features (a RAG chatbot on AWS Bedrock, AI translation and content pipelines) are already live in the product.

The role

You will own the Kidzapp backend (Python/Django REST APIs, admin, integrations, infrastructure) and the customer-facing website (Next.js) end to end. This is a full-time, fully remote position for an engineer based in Egypt, paid in USD, working directly with the founders.

What you will do

Own features end to end: scope with the founders, build across Django and Next.js, test, deploy to staging and production, and monitor afterwards.

Extend the versioned Django REST Framework APIs used by our iOS, Android and web clients, and the Django admin our operations team relies on.

Extend our RAG chatbot (Claude on AWS Bedrock plus vector search) into a booking assistant, and build new agents for merchant onboarding, content QA and internal operations.

Maintain OpenSearch indexing and search relevance.

Deploy through GitHub Actions and AWS CodeBuild to ECS, read New Relic and CloudWatch, and ﬁx slow queries and hot paths.

Use Claude Code or similar agents as your primary way of writing code, keep the repo agent-ready (, skills, hooks, MCP servers), and raise the bar for the team.

Our stack

Python, Django, Django REST Framework, Celery, Redis, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, OpenSearch, Next.js with React and TypeScript, Flutter mobile apps (iOS and Android), AWS (ECS, RDS, ElastiCache, Lambda, S3, CloudFront, Bedrock), Docker, GitHub Actions, New Relic, pytest and factory_boy. Solid React and Next.js: server-side rendering and static generation, routing, data fetching, SEO, internationalisation including RTL, and TypeScript as a default.
